# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Complex types and UDFs
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────

# Array type operations
data = [(1, ['Python', 'Spark', 'SQL']), (2, ['Java', 'Spark']), (3, ['Python'])]
df_arr = spark.createDataFrame(data, ['id', 'skills'])
df_arr.select('id', F.explode('skills').alias('skill')).show()
df_arr.select('id', F.size('skills').alias('num_skills')).show()

# Struct (nested) type
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType
schema = StructType([
    StructField('name', StringType()),
    StructField('address', StructType([
        StructField('city', StringType()),
        StructField('zip', StringType())
    ]))
])
nested_data = [('Alice', ('NYC', '10001')), ('Bob', ('SF', '94102'))]
df_nested = spark.createDataFrame(nested_data, schema)
df_nested.select('name', 'address.city', 'address.zip').show()

# UDF vs built-in function
from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
@udf(StringType())
def upper_custom(s):
    return s.upper() if s else None

# UDF (slower — avoid when possible)
emp.select('name', upper_custom('name').alias('upper_udf')).show(3)
# Built-in (faster — preferred)
emp.select('name', F.upper('name').alias('upper_builtin')).show(3)

PySpark — Interview Questions (Part 1)¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 How to create a DataFrame in PySpark? Create DataFrame • From list: spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
• From RDD: spark.createDataFrame(rdd, schema)
• From file: spark.read.csv(), .parquet(), .json()
• From Pandas: spark.createDataFrame(pandas_df)
2 StructType and StructField — defining schema? StructType, schema • StructType: container for list of StructFields
• StructField(name, dataType, nullable)
• Common types: StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType, ArrayType
• Manual schema preferred over inferSchema for production
3 select vs withColumn? Select, withColumn • select: choose/transform specific columns (returns new DF)
• withColumn: add or replace ONE column (returns full DF)
• select is better for multiple transformations
• withColumn one at a time can be slow (plan grows)
4 filter vs where — difference? Filter, where • Identical functionality — where is alias for filter
• df.filter(F.col('age') > 25) same as df.where('age > 25')
• filter with Column expression; where with SQL string
• Both return new DataFrame with matching rows
5 GroupBy + aggregation functions? GroupBy, agg • df.groupBy('col').agg(F.count('*'), F.avg('val'))
• Multiple aggs: F.sum(), F.min(), F.max(), F.count(), F.countDistinct()
• Alias results: .alias('avg_salary')
• Triggers shuffle (wide transformation)
6 All join types in PySpark? Join, types • inner: matching rows only
• left/right: all from one side + matching from other
• outer/full: all rows from both sides
• left_semi: left rows with match (no right columns)
• left_anti: left rows WITHOUT match
7 How does broadcast join work? Broadcast, join • Small table sent to all executors in memory
• Avoids shuffle — processes join locally per executor
• df1.join(F.broadcast(small_df), 'key')
• Auto-enabled when table < autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (10MB default)
8 Window functions — ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK? Window, rank • ROW_NUMBER: unique sequential number (no ties)
• RANK: same rank for ties, gaps after (1,2,2,4)
• DENSE_RANK: same rank for ties, no gaps (1,2,2,3)
• All require Window spec: Window.partitionBy().orderBy()
9 LAG and LEAD window functions? LAG, LEAD • LAG(col, n): value from n rows BEFORE current row
• LEAD(col, n): value from n rows AFTER current row
• Use for: comparing with previous/next values, running diffs
• Requires Window with ORDER BY
10 Explode, posexplode, explode_outer? Explode, array • explode: one row per array element (drops nulls/empties)
• posexplode: includes position index (pos, col)
• explode_outer: keeps null/empty rows as null
• Used with LATERAL VIEW in SQL or select in DataFrame API
11 How to read/write Parquet? CSV? JSON? Read, write, format • Parquet: spark.read.parquet('path') / df.write.parquet('path')
• CSV: spark.read.csv('path', header=True, inferSchema=True)
• JSON: spark.read.json('path') (one JSON per line)
• Mode: overwrite, append, ignore, error
12 Write modes in PySpark? Write mode • 'overwrite': replace existing data
• 'append': add to existing data
• 'ignore': skip if data exists
• 'error'/'errorifexists': fail if data exists (default)
13 PartitionBy in write — what does it do? PartitionBy, write • df.write.partitionBy('year', 'month').parquet('path')
• Creates directory structure: /year=2024/month=01/
• Enables partition pruning in read queries
• Choose low-cardinality columns (date parts, regions)
14 How to handle duplicate rows? Duplicate, dedup • df.distinct(): remove exact duplicate rows
• df.dropDuplicates(['col1', 'col2']): dedup on specific columns
• Window function approach: ROW_NUMBER + filter rank=1
• Window gives control over which duplicate to keep
15 How to handle null values? Null, fillna • df.na.fill({'col': default_val}): replace nulls
• df.na.drop(): remove rows with any null
• df.na.drop(subset=['col1']): null in specific columns only
• F.coalesce(col1, col2, lit('default')): first non-null
16 when/otherwise — conditional columns? When, otherwise • F.when(condition, value).when(cond2, val2).otherwise(default)
• Like SQL CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE
• Can be chained for multiple conditions
• Common for: categorization, flagging, data cleaning
17 TempView vs GlobalTempView? TempView, global • createOrReplaceTempView: visible in current SparkSession
• createGlobalTempView: visible across all sessions (spark.newSession())
• Access global: spark.sql('SELECT * FROM global_temp.view_name')
• Temp views lost when session ends
18 How to convert PySpark DataFrame to Pandas? toPandas, Arrow • pandas_df = spark_df.toPandas() — collects ALL data to driver
• DANGER: can OOM driver for large DataFrames
• Enable Arrow: spark.sql.execution.arrow.pyspark.enabled=true for faster transfer
• Always filter/sample before toPandas
19 What is SparkSQL? How to use? SparkSQL, query • SQL interface for querying DataFrames
• Register DataFrame as TempView → query with SQL
• spark.sql('SELECT * FROM employees WHERE age > 30')
• Same Catalyst optimizer as DataFrame API — same performance
20 printSchema vs dtypes? Schema, inspect • df.printSchema(): formatted tree showing column names, types, nullable
• df.dtypes: list of (name, type_string) tuples
• df.columns: just column names
• df.describe().show(): summary statistics

PySpark — Interview Questions (Part 2)¶

# Question Keywords Answer
21 How to rename multiple columns at once? Rename, columns • Loop: for old, new in mapping: df = df.withColumnRenamed(old, new)
• Select with alias: df.select([F.col(c).alias(new) for c, new in zip(...)])
• toDF: df.toDF(*new_names) (positional mapping)
• toDF is fastest for full rename
22 Cast column types? Cast, type • df.withColumn('age', F.col('age').cast('integer'))
• F.col('date_str').cast(DateType())
• Also: df.selectExpr("CAST(age AS INT)")
• Important for: CSV (all strings), type mismatches
23 Date functions in PySpark? Date, functions • F.current_date(), F.current_timestamp()
• F.to_date('str_col', 'yyyy-MM-dd')
• F.datediff('end', 'start'), F.date_add('col', n)
• F.year(), F.month(), F.dayofweek()
24 String functions in PySpark? String, functions • F.upper(), F.lower(), F.trim(), F.ltrim(), F.rtrim()
• F.concat(), F.concat_ws(sep, cols)
• F.substring('col', start, length)
• F.regexp_replace(), F.regexp_extract(), F.split()
25 How to pivot a DataFrame? Pivot • df.groupBy('dept').pivot('year').agg(F.sum('sales'))
• Converts rows to columns (year values become columns)
• Specify values: .pivot('year', [2022, 2023, 2024]) for efficiency
• Inverse: use stack() or unpivot (Spark 3.4+)
26 Union vs unionByName? Union, unionByName • union: combines by column position (must have same number)
• unionByName: combines by column name (order doesn't matter)
• unionByName(allowMissingColumns=True): fills missing with null
• unionByName preferred for safety
27 How to sample data? Sample, fraction • df.sample(fraction=0.1): 10% random sample
• df.sample(fraction=0.1, seed=42): reproducible
• df.sampleBy('col', fractions={'A': 0.1, 'B': 0.2}): stratified
• Useful for: development, testing, EDA
28 monotonically_increasing_id — what and when? Monotonic, ID • Generates unique (but not consecutive) 64-bit IDs
• Not guaranteed to be sequential — gaps allowed
• Each partition gets different range
• Use for: surrogate keys when ordering not critical
29 collect_list vs collect_set? Collect, list, set • collect_list: aggregates values into array (keeps duplicates, order varies)
• collect_set: aggregates into array (unique values only)
• df.groupBy('dept').agg(F.collect_list('name'))
• Caution: can be expensive for large groups (all values to one row)
30 How to create and use map columns? Map, create • F.create_map('key_col', 'value_col'): from two columns
• F.map_keys(col), F.map_values(col): extract keys/values
• Access value: F.col('map_col')['key'] or F.col('map_col').getItem('key')
• F.explode('map_col'): yields key, value columns
31 Salting technique for skewed joins? Salting, skew, join • Add random salt (0-n) to skewed key column
• Explode other side with same salt range
• Join on salted key → distributes evenly across partitions
• After join, remove salt and aggregate if needed
32 Caching best practices? Cache, best practice • Cache when: DataFrame reused multiple times in same job
• Don't cache: DataFrames used only once (wastes memory)
• Unpersist after use: df.unpersist()
• Check storage tab in Spark UI to monitor cached data
33 How to read data with custom schema? Schema, read • Define: schema = StructType([StructField('col', StringType())])
• Apply: spark.read.schema(schema).csv('file.csv')
• Manual schema avoids inferSchema overhead
• Required when: CSV columns are specific types, or reading empty files
34 What is repartition by column? Repartition, column • df.repartition(n, 'join_key'): hash-distribute by column
• Ensures same keys go to same partition
• Pre-repartition before: joins, groupBy (co-locates data)
• Reduces shuffle in subsequent operations
35 How to write output to single file? Single file, coalesce • df.coalesce(1).write.csv('out/', header=True)
• coalesce(1) = one partition = one output file
• Warning: bad for large data (no parallelism in write)
• Use only for small outputs (reports, exports)
36 Spark SQL EXPLAIN — reading the plan? Explain, plan • df.explain(True): shows parsed, analyzed, optimized, physical plans
• Physical plan: actual execution steps
• Look for: BroadcastHashJoin (good), SortMergeJoin (shuffle)
• WholeStageCodegen: Tungsten compilation
37 How to pass parameters to Spark jobs? Parameters, config • spark-submit --conf key=value
• spark.conf.set('key', 'value') in code
• Environment variables
• Airflow passes via --conf or Databricks widgets
38 What is schema merging? Schema merge, Parquet • Reading Parquet files with different schemas
• Enable: spark.read.option('mergeSchema', 'true').parquet('path')
• Unions all column schemas across files
• Missing columns filled with null
39 How to flatten nested JSON? Flatten, JSON • df.select('col.*') for StructType
• F.explode('array_col') for ArrayType
• Recursive: custom function to flatten all nesting levels
• F.from_json() to parse JSON string into struct
40 Performance tips for PySpark? Performance, tips • Use built-in functions over UDFs
• Broadcast small tables in joins
• Avoid collect() on large data
• Minimize shuffles: filter early, partition by join keys
• Enable AQE, tune spark.sql.shuffle.partitions

Part 8: Spark Streaming & Structured Streaming¶

Overview¶

Feature DStreams (Legacy) Structured Streaming (Modern)
API RDD-based micro-batches DataFrame/SQL-based
Optimization No Catalyst Full Catalyst + Tungsten
Exactly-once Complex to achieve Built-in with checkpointing
Event-time Not natively supported Watermark support
Status Deprecated in Spark 3.4+ Active development

Structured Streaming Processing Model¶

Source: Apache Spark — Structured Streaming Programming Guide

Output Modes¶

Mode Description Use Case
Append Only new rows added (no updates) Logs, raw ingestion
Complete Entire result table rewritten Aggregations with all data
Update Only changed rows written Aggregations (most common)

Triggers¶

Trigger Description
Default Process next batch as soon as previous finishes
Fixed interval trigger(processingTime='10 seconds')
Once trigger(once=True) — process all available, then stop
Available-now trigger(availableNow=True) — Spark 3.3+, like Once but better
Continuous trigger(continuous='1 second') — experimental low-latency

Watermarks¶

Watermarks handle late-arriving data in event-time processing:

df = spark.readStream.format('kafka').load()
df.withWatermark('event_time', '10 minutes') # tolerate 10 min late data
 .groupBy(F.window('event_time', '5 minutes'), 'user_id')
 .count()
  • Data arriving within watermark threshold → included in results
  • Data arriving after threshold → dropped
  • Enables Spark to clean up old state

Spark Streaming — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is Structured Streaming? How different from DStreams? Structured, DStreams • DataFrame/SQL API for stream processing (modern)
• DStreams: RDD-based micro-batch (legacy, deprecated Spark 3.4+)
• Structured Streaming uses Catalyst optimizer
• Built-in exactly-once, watermarks, event-time support
2 Unbounded table model in Structured Streaming? Unbounded, table • Treat streaming data as rows appending to infinite table
• Queries run incrementally — process new data each trigger
• Same query works for both batch and streaming
• Result table updated incrementally
3 Output modes — append vs complete vs update? Output mode • Append: only new rows (no aggregations or simple ones)
• Complete: entire result table rewritten (aggregations)
• Update: only changed rows written (most common for aggs)
• Mode depends on query type and sink capabilities
4 What is a watermark? Why needed? Watermark, late data • Threshold for how late event-time data is accepted
• df.withWatermark('event_time', '10 minutes')
• Enables Spark to drop old state (bounded memory)
• Without watermark: state grows unbounded → OOM
5 Triggers in Structured Streaming? Trigger, processing • Default: process ASAP after previous batch
• Fixed interval: trigger(processingTime='10 seconds')
• Once: process all available, stop (batch-like)
• AvailableNow (Spark 3.3+): improved Once trigger
• Continuous: experimental ≈1ms latency
6 Checkpointing — why critical for streaming? Checkpoint, fault • Saves query progress + state to durable storage (S3/HDFS)
• Enables exactly-once semantics on restart
• Stores: source offsets, operator state, output commits
• Required for production streaming queries
7 How to read from Kafka in Structured Streaming? Kafka, source • spark.readStream.format('kafka').option('subscribe', 'topic').load()
• Produces DataFrame with key, value, timestamp columns
• Parse value: F.from_json(F.col('value').cast('string'), schema)
• Offsets managed automatically via checkpointing
8 How to write to Delta Lake from streaming? Delta, sink • df.writeStream.format('delta').start('/path')
• Must specify checkpointLocation
• Supports: append and complete modes
• Delta ensures ACID + exactly-once writes
9 Micro-batch vs continuous processing? Micro-batch, continuous • Micro-batch: default, processes data in small batches (≈100ms+)
• Continuous: experimental, true streaming (≈1ms latency)
• Micro-batch: exactly-once guarantee
• Continuous: at-least-once only (limited operations)
10 Window functions in streaming? Window, event-time • Tumbling: F.window('event_time', '5 minutes') — non-overlapping
• Sliding: F.window('event_time', '10 minutes', '5 minutes') — overlapping
• Session: group by activity gaps (Spark 3.2+)
• Always use with watermark for bounded state
11 How to handle late data in streaming? Late data, watermark • Define watermark: data arriving within threshold is included
• Data beyond watermark is silently dropped
• Larger watermark = more late data accepted, more state
• Balance: latency vs completeness
12 Exactly-once semantics — how achieved? Exactly-once • Checkpointing: tracks processed offsets
• Idempotent sinks: Delta, Kafka (with unique keys)
• On restart: replay from last committed offset
• Requires: checkpointLocation + idempotent sink
13 stateful vs stateless stream operations? Stateful, stateless • Stateless: map, filter, select (no memory of past data)
• Stateful: groupBy, window, join (maintains state across batches)
• Stateful requires: watermarks (to bound state), checkpointing
• State stored in RocksDB-based state store
14 Stream-stream join? Stream, join • Join two streaming DataFrames on key + time conditions
• Requires watermarks on both sides
• Inner join: output when both match within watermark
• Outer join: output after watermark expires if no match
15 Stream-static join? Stream, static, join • Join streaming DataFrame with a static (batch) DataFrame
• Static side: read once, cached or re-read each trigger
• No watermark needed for static side
• Common: enrich stream events with lookup tables
16 foreachBatch — what and when? foreachBatch • Apply arbitrary batch logic to each micro-batch DataFrame
• query = df.writeStream.foreachBatch(process_fn).start()
• Use for: JDBC writes, custom sinks, multi-destination writes
• process_fn receives: (batch_df, batch_id)
17 foreach vs foreachBatch? foreach, foreachBatch • foreach: processes row-by-row (use for row-level logic)
• foreachBatch: processes entire micro-batch as DataFrame (preferred)
• foreachBatch is more efficient (batch operations)
• foreach used when: row-level custom sinks
18 Rate source — what is it? Rate, testing • Built-in test source generating rows at configurable rate
• spark.readStream.format('rate').option('rowsPerSecond', 100).load()
• Produces: timestamp, value columns
• Use for: testing streaming queries without real sources
19 How to monitor streaming queries? Monitor, metrics • query.status: current status (active trigger info)
• query.lastProgress: detailed metrics (input rows, processing time)
• query.awaitTermination(): block until query stops
• StreamingQueryListener for custom monitoring
20 Structured Streaming on Databricks? Databricks, streaming • Auto-optimized with Delta Lake as sink
• Autoloader: spark.readStream.format('cloudFiles') for file ingestion
• DLT (Delta Live Tables) for managed streaming pipelines
• Built-in monitoring, schema inference, auto-scaling
21 maxFilesPerTrigger and maxOffsetsPerTrigger? Rate limiting • maxFilesPerTrigger: limit files read per batch (file sources)
• maxOffsetsPerTrigger: limit records per batch (Kafka)
• Use to: control processing rate, prevent OOM
• Start conservative, increase as pipeline stabilizes
22 State store in Structured Streaming? State, store • Manages state for stateful operations (aggregations, joins)
• Default: HDFS-backed state store
• Databricks: RocksDB-based state store (faster, more scalable)
• State grows with unique keys — watermark bounds it
23 How to restart a failed streaming query? Restart, recovery • Query restarts from last checkpoint (exactly-once)
• Checkpoints store: offsets, state snapshots, commit log
• Must use same checkpoint location on restart
• Schema changes may require: new checkpoint (reset state)
24 Deduplication in streaming? Deduplicate, stream • df.dropDuplicates(['event_id']) with watermark
• Maintains set of seen IDs in state store
• Watermark controls how long IDs are tracked
• Without watermark: state grows unbounded
25 Batch vs stream unification with Delta? Batch, stream, Delta • Same Delta table serves both batch and stream queries
• spark.readStream.format('delta') reads as stream
• spark.read.format('delta') reads as batch
• Enables: lambda architecture replacement, incremental ETL

Part 9: Delta Lake & Modern Data Lakes¶

What is Delta Lake?¶

Delta Lake is an open-source storage layer that brings ACID transactions, schema enforcement, and time travel to data lakes. It sits on top of Parquet and adds a transaction log (_delta_log) for reliability.

Delta Lake vs Traditional Data Lake¶

Feature Raw Parquet/CSV Lake Delta Lake
ACID Transactions Atomic commits
Schema Enforcement Silent corruption Rejects bad schemas
Schema Evolution Manual mergeSchema option
Time Travel VERSION AS OF / TIMESTAMP
UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE Rewrite entire dataset Native DML support
Data Skipping Min/max stats per file
Concurrent Writes Corruption risk Optimistic concurrency
Streaming + Batch Separate pipelines Unified on same table

Transaction Log (_delta_log)¶

Source: Databricks — Unpacking the Transaction Log

Each commit is a JSON file recording file-level actions (add/remove). Checkpoints are Parquet summaries for faster log replay. This enables ACID, time travel, and concurrent access.

Key Operations¶

Operation SQL PySpark Purpose
MERGE INTO MERGE INTO target USING source ON condition WHEN MATCHED THEN ... DeltaTable.merge() Upsert (insert+update)
UPDATE UPDATE table SET col=val WHERE ... deltaTable.update(condition, set) Modify rows
DELETE DELETE FROM table WHERE ... deltaTable.delete(condition) Remove rows
OPTIMIZE OPTIMIZE table — Compact small files
ZORDER OPTIMIZE table ZORDER BY (col) — Co-locate data for faster queries
VACUUM VACUUM table RETAIN 168 HOURS — Remove old files

Schema Enforcement vs Evolution¶

Feature Enforcement Evolution
Purpose Reject incompatible writes Allow new columns
Default Always ON Must enable
Enable Automatic .option('mergeSchema', 'true')
Use case Prevent corruption Evolving data sources

Time Travel¶

-- Query by version number
SELECT * FROM my_table VERSION AS OF 5;

-- Query by timestamp
SELECT * FROM my_table TIMESTAMP AS OF '2025-01-01T12:00:00';

-- PySpark
spark.read.format('delta').option('versionAsOf', 5).load('/path')
spark.read.format('delta').option('timestampAsOf', '2025-01-01').load('/path')

-- View history
DESCRIBE HISTORY my_table;

Advanced Features¶

Feature Description
Deletion Vectors Mark deleted rows without rewriting files (faster DML)
Liquid Clustering Auto-organize data layout (replaces manual ZORDER)
CDF (Change Data Feed) Track row-level changes between versions
Generated Columns Auto-computed columns from expressions
Constraints NOT NULL, CHECK constraints for data quality

Delta Lake examples (commented — need delta-spark package installed)

Delta Lake — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is Delta Lake? How different from raw Parquet? Delta, Parquet • Open-source storage layer with ACID transactions on data lakes
• Adds transaction log (_delta_log) on top of Parquet
• Supports: DML (UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE), schema enforcement, time travel
• Raw Parquet: no transactions, no DML, no versioning
2 How does Delta Lake achieve ACID compliance? ACID, transaction log • Atomicity: each write creates commit file; partial writes never visible
• Consistency: schema enforcement ensures valid writes
• Isolation: optimistic concurrency control (conflict detection at commit)
• Durability: files stored in durable cloud storage (S3/ADLS)
3 Explain the Delta transaction log (_delta_log). Transaction log • Folder storing sequential JSON commit files + checkpoints
• Each commit: records file actions (add, remove Parquet files)
• Checkpoints: Parquet files summarizing log for faster replay
• Source of truth: enables ACID, time travel, concurrent access
4 What is time travel in Delta? How to use? Time travel, version • Query previous versions by version number or timestamp
• SELECT * FROM table VERSION AS OF 5
• spark.read.format('delta').option('versionAsOf', 5).load(path)
• Use for: auditing, debugging, reproducible ML, rollback
5 Schema enforcement vs schema evolution? Schema, enforcement • Enforcement: rejects writes with incompatible schema (always on)
• Evolution: allow adding new columns with mergeSchema option
• Enforcement prevents data corruption
• Evolution handles evolving data sources (new fields)
6 UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE INTO in Delta? DML, MERGE • UPDATE: modify rows matching condition
• DELETE: remove rows matching condition
• MERGE INTO: upsert — insert/update/delete in one atomic op
• All leverage transaction log for ACID compliance
7 What is OPTIMIZE? Why needed? OPTIMIZE, compaction • Compacts many small Parquet files into fewer larger ones
• Small files from streaming/incremental writes degrade performance
• OPTIMIZE sales — rewrites table with optimal file sizes
• Schedule regularly for Silver/Gold layers
8 What is ZORDER? How to use? ZORDER, clustering • Co-locates related data within files for efficient data skipping
• OPTIMIZE sales ZORDER BY (customer_id, region)
• Improves performance for queries filtering on ZORDER columns
• Combine with OPTIMIZE for maximum benefit
9 OPTIMIZE + ZORDER vs liquid clustering? Liquid clustering • ZORDER: one-time optimization, needs periodic re-run
• Liquid clustering: automatically maintains data layout during writes
• Liquid clustering replaces manual OPTIMIZE + ZORDER
• Liquid clustering is next-gen, reducing operational overhead
10 What is VACUUM? Why important? VACUUM, retention • Removes old Parquet files no longer referenced by transaction log
• VACUUM table RETAIN 168 HOURS (default 7 days retention)
• Without VACUUM: storage costs grow indefinitely
• Caution: VACUUM removes time travel ability for vacuumed versions
11 What are deletion vectors? Deletion vectors • Mark deleted rows without rewriting entire Parquet files
• Separate index file tracks which rows are deleted
• Much faster DML: skip expensive file rewrites
• Physical removal happens later during compaction
12 CDF (Change Data Feed) — what and why? CDF, change feed • Track row-level changes (insert, update, delete) between versions
• SELECT * FROM table_changes('table', start, end)
• Use for: incremental ETL, streaming updates, ML feature refresh
• Avoids reprocessing full dataset
13 Generated columns in Delta? Generated, column • Auto-computed columns from expressions on other columns
• year INT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (YEAR(sale_date))
• Useful for: partition columns derived from timestamps
• Ensures consistency, reduces user error
14 How Delta handles concurrent writes? Concurrent, OCC • Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC)
• Writer reads latest snapshot, prepares changes, validates at commit
• If conflict: transaction fails and retries with latest version
• Readers always see consistent snapshot (isolation)
15 Delta tables in streaming workloads? Streaming, Delta • Delta table as both source and sink for Structured Streaming
• readStream: reads new commits incrementally
• writeStream: writes with checkpointing + exactly-once
• Unifies batch and stream on same data
16 Managed vs external Delta tables? Managed, external • Managed: Databricks controls storage; DROP deletes data + metadata
• External: user specifies LOCATION; DROP deletes metadata only
• External for: shared data across tools/platforms
• Managed for: Databricks-only internal projects
17 How does data skipping work in Delta? Data skipping, stats • Delta stores min/max stats per column per file in _delta_log
• Queries with filters skip files outside range
• Automatic — no manual setup needed
• Enhanced by ZORDER (improves data locality)
18 Delta Lake small files problem? Small files, compact • Streaming/micro-batch writes create many small files
• Too many files → slow queries (metadata overhead)
• Solution: OPTIMIZE (manual) or auto-compaction (Databricks)
• Target file size: ~256 MB for optimal performance
19 Constraints in Delta Lake? Constraints, quality • NOT NULL: prevent null values in specific columns
• CHECK: validate column values with expressions
• ALTER TABLE t ADD CONSTRAINT chk CHECK (age > 0)
• Enforcement: writes violating constraints fail
20 Delta vs Iceberg vs Hudi? Delta, Iceberg, Hudi • Delta: Databricks-native, rich ACID, mature MERGE, Photon integration
• Iceberg: multi-engine (Spark, Flink, Trino), hidden partitioning
• Hudi: strong CDC/upsert support, record-level indexing
• Delta most popular in Databricks ecosystem
21 How to convert Parquet to Delta? Convert, Parquet • CONVERT TO DELTA parquet.\/path/to/parquet_table``
• Creates _delta_log on existing Parquet files (in-place)
• No data rewrite — adds metadata layer only
• Enables Delta features on existing data
22 Delta Lake best practices for production? Production, best practice • OPTIMIZE + ZORDER regularly for query performance
• VACUUM to control storage costs
• Monitor _delta_log size with DESCRIBE HISTORY
• Set NOT NULL/CHECK constraints for data quality
23 Medallion architecture (Bronze/Silver/Gold)? Medallion, Bronze • Bronze: raw ingested data (CSV, JSON, logs) — minimal processing
• Silver: cleaned, deduplicated, schema-enforced — analytics-ready
• Gold: aggregated, business-specific KPIs — dashboards/ML
• Flow: Raw → Cleansed → Business-ready
24 What is DESCRIBE HISTORY in Delta? DESCRIBE, HISTORY • Shows full history of operations on a Delta table
• Includes: version, timestamp, operation, user, parameters
• Useful for: auditing, debugging, compliance (GDPR/SOX)
• SQL: DESCRIBE HISTORY my_table
25 How to rollback a Delta table? Rollback, restore • RESTORE TABLE table TO VERSION AS OF n
• Restores table to a previous version
• Use for: accidental deletes, corruption recovery
• Only works within VACUUM retention period

Part 10: Databricks Platform¶

Overview¶

Databricks is a unified analytics platform built on Apache Spark, providing cloud-based clusters, collaborative notebooks, Delta Lake integration, and enterprise governance via Unity Catalog. It implements the Lakehouse architecture.

Architecture¶

Source: Databricks — Lakehouse Architecture

Key Components¶

Component Description
Workspace Container for notebooks, libraries, dashboards, repos
Cluster Managed Spark environment — auto-scaling, auto-termination
DBFS Databricks File System — abstraction over cloud storage
Unity Catalog Centralized governance: RBAC, data lineage, audit logs
Photon Native C++ vectorized query engine (10x faster SQL)
Delta Live Tables (DLT) Managed pipeline framework with quality expectations
Autoloader Incremental file ingestion from cloud storage
MLflow ML lifecycle: tracking, models, registry, projects
SQL Warehouses Serverless SQL compute for BI and analytics
Repos Git integration (GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps)
Widgets Parameterize notebooks (dropdown, text, multiselect)
Secrets Secure credential management (dbutils.secrets)

Cluster Types¶

Type Description Use Case
All-Purpose (Interactive) Long-running, multi-user attached Development, exploration, notebooks
Job Cluster Ephemeral — created per job, terminated after Production ETL, scheduled pipelines
SQL Warehouse Serverless compute for SQL queries BI dashboards, Tableau, Power BI

Databricks vs Open-Source Spark¶

Feature Open-Source Spark Databricks
Setup Manual cluster + config Managed, auto-scaling
Performance JVM-based Photon engine (C++, 10x faster)
Storage HDFS, S3 (raw) Delta Lake (ACID, governance)
Governance None Unity Catalog (RBAC, lineage)
Collaboration Separate tools Built-in notebooks, dashboards
MLOps Manual MLflow Integrated MLflow + Feature Store

Databricks Platform — Interview Questions (Part 1)¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is Databricks? How different from Spark? Databricks, Spark • Unified analytics platform built on Spark (managed service)
• Adds: auto-scaling clusters, notebooks, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog
• Photon engine for 10x faster SQL
• Open-source Spark = engine; Databricks = platform
2 Databricks architecture — control plane vs data plane? Architecture, planes • Control plane: hosted by Databricks (UI, notebook server, jobs scheduler)
• Data plane: runs in customer's cloud (clusters, storage)
• Data never leaves customer's cloud account
• Separation ensures security and compliance
3 What is a Databricks Workspace? Workspace • Top-level container for all Databricks assets
• Contains: notebooks, libraries, repos, dashboards, experiments
• Multiple workspaces per organization for isolation
• Users, groups, permissions managed at workspace level
4 What is DBFS? How to use it? DBFS, file system • Databricks File System — abstraction over cloud storage
• Access: dbutils.fs.ls('/'), /dbfs/ mount point
• Maps to S3/ADLS/GCS transparently
• Use for: temporary files, shared data; prefer Unity Catalog for production
5 Unity Catalog — what and why? Unity Catalog, governance • Centralized data governance across clouds and Databricks workspaces
• Features: RBAC, column-level security, data lineage, audit logs
• Hierarchy: Account → Metastore → Catalog → Schema → Table
• Single pane for governance across all data assets
6 Databricks Runtime vs open-source Spark? Runtime, Spark • Databricks Runtime = Spark + performance optimizations
• Includes: Photon engine, Delta Lake, auto-optimizations
• Runtime ML: adds ML libraries (MLflow, TensorFlow, PyTorch)
• Standard Runtime: general-purpose compute
7 Job cluster vs interactive cluster? Job, interactive • Job cluster: ephemeral — created per job, auto-terminated
• Interactive: long-running, multiple users attached
• Job clusters: cost-optimized for production
• Interactive: higher cost risk if left running
8 How does cluster autoscaling work? Autoscaling, cluster • Set min/max workers; Databricks adds/removes based on load
• Scale up: when tasks are queued
• Scale down: when executors idle beyond threshold
• Optimized autoscaling: faster scale-down with spot instances
9 What is Photon engine? Photon, C++ • Native vectorized query engine written in C++
• Runs underneath Databricks SQL and Spark SQL
• Up to 10x faster than JVM-based Spark execution
• Optimized for modern CPUs (SIMD, cache-aware)
10 Delta Live Tables (DLT) — what is it? DLT, pipeline • Managed pipeline framework for building Delta tables
• Declarative syntax: define what, not how
• Built-in: data quality expectations, auto-retries, monitoring
• Difference: Delta Table = storage format; DLT = pipeline framework
11 DLT vs regular Delta Tables? DLT, Delta, compare • DLT: managed pipeline with quality rules, auto orchestration
• Regular Delta: manual ETL, manual orchestration
• DLT: @dlt.table decorator, LIVE syntax
• DLT better for production-grade, governed pipelines
12 What is Autoloader? How different from Structured Streaming? Autoloader, CloudFiles • Optimized incremental file ingestion from cloud storage
• spark.readStream.format('cloudFiles').load(path)
• Auto-discovers new files via notifications or directory listing
• Structured Streaming is general-purpose; Autoloader is file-specific
13 MLflow in Databricks — components? MLflow, ML • Tracking: log metrics, parameters, artifacts from experiments
• Models: standard packaging format for deployment
• Registry: model versions, stages (Staging → Production)
• Projects: reproducible code environment
14 Databricks Repos — Git integration? Repos, Git • Clone GitHub/GitLab/Azure DevOps repos into workspace
• Supports: pull, commit, branch, merge
• Enables CI/CD: push code → automated testing → deployment
• Version control for notebooks and Python files
15 Databricks Widgets — what are they? Widgets, parameters • UI input controls in notebooks (dropdown, text, multiselect)
• dbutils.widgets.text('year', '2025', 'Enter Year')
• Get value: dbutils.widgets.get('year')
• Use for: parameterized notebooks, dynamic job execution
16 How to manage secrets in Databricks? Secrets, credentials • Databricks Secrets: securely store API keys, passwords, tokens
• Access: dbutils.secrets.get(scope='my_scope', key='db_password')
• Backends: Databricks-backed or Azure Key Vault/AWS Secrets Manager
• Never hardcode credentials in notebooks
17 Databricks SQL Warehouses? SQL Warehouse • Serverless compute layer for BI and SQL workloads
• Query Delta tables with ANSI SQL
• Connect BI tools: Power BI, Tableau, Looker
• Features: auto-scaling, caching, role-based access
18 Databricks SQL vs Spark SQL? SQL, compare • Databricks SQL: analyst-friendly, runs on SQL Warehouses (serverless)
• Spark SQL: developer/engineer tool, runs on Spark clusters
• Databricks SQL: native dashboards + external BI tools
• Spark SQL: typically inside ETL pipelines
19 Lakehouse architecture? Lakehouse • Combines data lake flexibility with warehouse reliability
• ONE platform for: ETL, BI, ML, streaming
• Open storage (Delta Lake on Parquet) + ACID + governance
• Replaces separate lake + warehouse = lower cost, less duplication
20 Bronze, Silver, Gold layers in Databricks? Medallion, BSG • Bronze: raw ingested data (minimal processing)
• Silver: cleaned, deduplicated, schema-enforced
• Gold: aggregated business KPIs for dashboards/ML
• Follow medallion architecture for quality progression
21 How to monitor and debug jobs? Monitor, debug • Job UI: view run status, logs, failure points
• Spark UI: stages, tasks, shuffle, GC metrics
• Cluster logs: driver/executor log files
• Set alerts for job failures (email/Slack)
22 Cost optimization strategies? Cost, optimize • Use job clusters (ephemeral) instead of interactive for production
• Enable auto-termination for idle clusters
• Use spot/preemptible VMs for non-critical jobs
• Run OPTIMIZE + VACUUM to reduce storage costs
23 Databricks Workflows? Workflows, orchestration • Orchestration service for scheduling and chaining tasks
• Chain: notebooks, SQL, Python, dbt, JARs into DAGs
• Task dependencies, conditional execution, retries
• REST API and CI/CD integration
24 Cluster lifecycle stages? Cluster, lifecycle • Creation → Initialization → Running → Auto-scaling → Idle Timeout → Termination
• Job clusters: terminated after job completes
• Interactive: manual or auto-terminated
• Metadata/logs retained after termination
25 Cluster modes — Standard vs High Concurrency? Cluster mode • Standard: single-user or multi-user, general purpose
• High Concurrency: multi-user isolation, table ACLs
• Single Node: no workers, debugging/small tasks
• Standard most common; HC for shared team clusters

Databricks Platform — Interview Questions (Part 2)¶

# Question Keywords Answer
26 Managed vs external tables in Databricks? Managed, external • Managed: Databricks controls storage; DROP deletes data + metadata
• External: data in external location (S3/ADLS); DROP keeps data
• External for shared data across platforms
• Managed: CREATE TABLE t USING DELTA; External: LOCATION '/path'
27 Caching vs materialized views? Cache, materialized • Caching: temporary in-memory boost (CACHE TABLE, df.cache())
• Materialized view: precomputed, persistent query result
• MV auto-refreshed; cache lost on cluster restart
• MV for repeated BI queries; cache for iterative ML
28 GDPR/PII compliance in Databricks? GDPR, PII • Classify and tag PII columns (Unity Catalog)
• Row/column-level security: restrict access by role
• Data masking/tokenization for sensitive values
• Right to be Forgotten: DELETE + VACUUM in Delta
29 Databricks Secrets scopes — types? Secrets, scope • Databricks-backed: stored and encrypted in Databricks
• Azure Key Vault: external integration with Azure
• AWS Secrets Manager: external integration with AWS
• Apply RBAC on secret scopes for access control
30 Job scheduling and retries? Scheduling, retries • Schedule via UI, REST API, or CI/CD
• Supports cron expressions and event-triggered
• Retry policies: max attempts, delay between retries
• Task dependencies for DAG-like workflows
31 Data skipping and ZORDER? Skipping, ZORDER • Data skipping: auto uses min/max stats per file
• ZORDER: co-locates related values in same files
• Combined: dramatically reduces data scanned
• Run OPTIMIZE + ZORDER on frequently filtered columns
32 How to integrate with Azure/AWS/GCP services? Integration, cloud • Azure: ADLS Gen2, Synapse, Key Vault, Event Hub
• AWS: S3, Redshift, IAM roles, Kinesis
• GCP: GCS, BigQuery, Pub/Sub
• Unity Catalog for cross-cloud governance
33 Catalyst and Tungsten in Databricks? Catalyst, Tungsten • Catalyst: query optimizer (predicate pushdown, join ordering)
• Tungsten: execution engine (off-heap memory, WSCG, codegen)
• Databricks adds Photon on top (C++ vectorized execution)
• Catalyst = planner, Tungsten = JVM executor, Photon = C++ executor
34 OOM errors in Databricks — how to debug? OOM, debug • Check Spark UI: skewed partitions, large shuffles
• Optimize joins: broadcast small tables
• Repartition: balance partition sizes
• Increase executor memory or scale cluster
35 Partitioning and bucketing best practices? Partition, bucket • Partition on time-based columns (date, month)
• Keep partitions 1GB–2GB each (avoid over-partitioning)
• Bucket on join keys for repeated joins
• Combine with OPTIMIZE + ZORDER for query speed
36 Delta versioning and time travel in Databricks? Versioning, history • _delta_log stores full history of table changes
• Time travel: VERSION AS OF, TIMESTAMP AS OF
• DESCRIBE HISTORY: audit all operations
• RESTORE TABLE: rollback to previous version
37 Streaming pipelines in Databricks? Streaming, pipeline • Structured Streaming + Delta Lake as default pattern
• Autoloader: incremental file ingestion from cloud storage
• DLT: managed streaming with quality expectations
• Sources: Kafka, Event Hubs, Kinesis, file sources
38 Community Edition vs Enterprise? Community, Enterprise • Community: free, single-node, limited storage, learning only
• Enterprise: multi-node, full features (DLT, Photon, MLflow)
• Enterprise: RBAC, encryption, audit logs, Unity Catalog
• Community for learning; Enterprise for production
39 Notebook collaboration features? Collaboration, notebook • Real-time co-editing (Google Docs-like)
• Inline comments for peer review
• Version history: track and restore previous versions
• Granular permissions: Read, Run, Edit, Manage
40 Databricks data governance — Unity Catalog features? Governance, UC • Centralized metastore across workspaces/clouds
• Fine-grained access control (table, column, row level)
• Automated data lineage tracking
• Audit logging for compliance (GDPR, SOX, HIPAA)
41 What is the medallion architecture pipeline in practice? Medallion, pipeline • Bronze notebook: Autoloader → raw Delta table
• Silver notebook: clean, validate, join → curated Delta
• Gold notebook: aggregate, model → BI/ML-ready
• DLT can automate entire medallion pipeline
42 How to optimize joins and shuffles in Databricks? Join, shuffle • Broadcast join for small tables (<10MB)
• Bucketing: pre-hash large tables on join key
• AQE: auto-converts to broadcast, handles skew
• Repartition on join key before join
43 Databricks init scripts? Init scripts • Shell scripts that run when cluster starts
• Install custom libraries, configure environment
• Types: cluster-scoped or global
• Stored in DBFS or workspace files
44 dbutils — common utilities? dbutils • dbutils.fs: file system operations
• dbutils.secrets: access credentials securely
• dbutils.widgets: notebook parameterization
• dbutils.notebook.run(): run child notebooks
45 How to handle schema evolution in Databricks Delta? Schema evolution • Add columns: .option('mergeSchema', 'true')
• Global: spark.databricks.delta.schema.autoMerge.enabled = true
• Schema enforcement blocks writes with mismatched types
• Use OVERWRITE for full schema replacement
46 Databricks pools — what are they? Pools, instance • Pre-provisioned idle instances for faster cluster startup
• Reduce cluster creation time from minutes to seconds
• Share across multiple clusters
• Configure: min/max idle instances
47 Libraries management in Databricks? Libraries, install • Cluster libraries: installed on all nodes of a cluster
• Notebook-scoped: %pip install package_name
• Workspace libraries: available across clusters
• Requirements.txt or init scripts for reproducibility
48 Databricks Connect — what is it? Connect, IDE • Run Spark code from local IDE (VSCode, PyCharm) on Databricks cluster
• Develop in local environment, execute on cloud
• Version 2: uses Spark Connect protocol (Spark 3.4+)
• Great for: debugging, testing, CI/CD integration
49 Real-time use cases on Databricks? Real-time, use case • Fraud detection: Kafka → real-time ML scoring
• IoT analytics: stream sensor data → anomaly detection
• Clickstream: user event tracking → personalization
• Financial: stock trades → predictive analytics
50 Future roadmap of Databricks? Roadmap, future • Expanding Unity Catalog across data, AI, and ML
• More serverless offerings (SQL, ML workloads)
• Enhanced AI/LLM integration (MosaicML, AI agents)
• Tighter integration with cloud ecosystems (Azure Fabric, AWS)

Part 11: Apache Kafka¶

Overview¶

Apache Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform for high-throughput, fault-tolerant, real-time data pipelines and event-driven architectures.

Architecture¶

Source: TutorialsPoint — Apache Kafka

Core Concepts¶

Concept Description
Topic Named stream of messages (like a table)
Partition Ordered, immutable sequence within a topic; enables parallelism
Offset Position of a message within a partition (monotonically increasing)
Broker Kafka server that stores data and serves clients
Producer Publishes messages to topics
Consumer Reads messages from topics
Consumer Group Group of consumers sharing partition load
Replication Factor Number of copies per partition (typically 3)
Leader/Follower One leader handles reads/writes; followers replicate
ISR (In-Sync Replicas) Followers fully caught up with leader

Kafka Ecosystem¶

Component Purpose
Kafka Connect Pre-built connectors for data ingestion/egestion (JDBC, S3, ElasticSearch)
Kafka Streams Stream processing library (Java) for transformations
Schema Registry Centralized schema management (Avro, JSON Schema, Protobuf)
ksqlDB SQL engine for stream processing on Kafka
KRaft Kafka Raft — replaces ZooKeeper for metadata management (Kafka 3.3+)

Apache Kafka — Interview Questions (Part 1)¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is Apache Kafka? Why is it popular? Kafka, streaming • Distributed event streaming platform for real-time data pipelines
• High throughput: millions of events/second
• Durable: persists messages to disk with replication
• Decouples producers and consumers (pub/sub model)
2 Kafka architecture — brokers, topics, partitions? Architecture • Cluster: multiple brokers (servers) for fault tolerance
• Topic: named stream; divided into partitions
• Partition: ordered, immutable append log
• Messages identified by offset within partition
3 What is a Kafka partition? Why needed? Partition • Parallel unit within a topic (each on potentially different broker)
• Enables horizontal scaling of reads/writes
• Each partition: ordered, immutable sequence
• More partitions = more consumer parallelism
4 Consumer groups — how do they work? Consumer group • Group of consumers sharing partitions of a topic
• Each partition assigned to exactly one consumer in group
• Multiple groups can independently consume same topic
• Rebalance: partitions redistributed when consumers join/leave
5 Kafka offset — what is it? How managed? Offset • Sequential position of message within partition
• Consumer tracks its offset to resume reading
• Offsets committed to __consumer_offsets topic
• Auto-commit or manual commit for at-least-once/exactly-once
6 Producer — how does it write to partitions? Producer, partitioning • Key-based: hash(key) % num_partitions (same key → same partition)
• Round-robin: no key specified → distribute evenly
• Custom partitioner: implement custom logic
• Key-based ensures ordering per key
7 What is replication in Kafka? Leader vs follower? Replication, leader • Each partition replicated across N brokers (replication factor)
• Leader: handles all reads/writes for that partition
• Followers: replicate data from leader (in ISR = in-sync replicas)
• If leader fails → one ISR follower promoted to leader
8 What is ISR (In-Sync Replicas)? ISR, replicas • Set of replicas fully caught up with the leader
• Messages only considered committed when all ISR replicas ACK
• Falling behind: replica removed from ISR
• min.insync.replicas: minimum ISR for writes to succeed
9 Kafka delivery guarantees — at-most, at-least, exactly-once? Delivery, semantics • At-most-once: fire and forget (possible loss, no duplication)
• At-least-once: retry on failure (no loss, possible duplicates)
• Exactly-once: idempotent producer + transactions (no loss, no duplication)
• Exactly-once requires: enable.idempotence=true
10 Producer ACKs — 0, 1, all? ACK, producer • acks=0: no acknowledgment (fastest, fire-and-forget)
• acks=1: leader ACKs (balanced — data may be lost if leader crashes)
• acks=all (-1): all ISR ACK (safest, highest latency)
• Production: acks=all + min.insync.replicas=2
11 Kafka Connect — what and why? Connect, connectors • Framework for pre-built data integration connectors
• Source connectors: pull data into Kafka (JDBC, PostgreSQL, S3)
• Sink connectors: push data from Kafka (HDFS, ElasticSearch, Delta)
• Handles: offset tracking, schema management, fault tolerance
12 Schema Registry — purpose? Schema Registry • Centralized schema management for Kafka topics
• Supports: Avro, JSON Schema, Protobuf
• Ensures compatibility: backward, forward, full
• Prevents breaking changes from being published
13 KRaft — replacing ZooKeeper? KRaft, ZooKeeper • Kafka Raft: built-in metadata management (Kafka 3.3+)
• Replaces ZooKeeper dependency for controller election and metadata
• Simpler deployment (no separate ZooKeeper cluster)
• Better scaling and faster failover
14 Kafka Streams — what is it? Streams, library • Java library for building stream processing applications
• Lightweight: no separate cluster needed (runs in app process)
• Features: joins, aggregations, windowing, stateful processing
• Alternative to: Spark Streaming, Flink (simpler deployment)
15 ksqlDB — what is it? ksqlDB, SQL • SQL engine for stream processing directly on Kafka
• CREATE STREAM ... AS SELECT ... FROM ...
• No coding required — SQL-only stream transformations
• Best for: simple transforms, aggregations, joins
16 Topic retention policies? Retention, cleanup • Time-based: retention.ms=604800000 (7 days default)
• Size-based: retention.bytes=1073741824 (1 GB per partition)
• Compaction: keep latest value per key only
• Compaction useful for: changelogs, configuration topics
17 Log compaction — what and when? Compaction, log • Keeps only the LATEST value for each key (removes old versions)
• Used for: changelog topics, KVstore-like behavior
• Different from deletion: compaction retains latest state
• Enable: cleanup.policy=compact
18 Consumer lag — what is it? How to monitor? Lag, monitoring • Difference between latest offset and consumer's committed offset
• High lag = consumer falling behind producers
• Monitor with: kafka-consumer-groups.sh, Prometheus, Burrow
• Solutions: add consumers, increase partitions, optimize processing
19 Kafka message ordering guarantees? Ordering, guarantee • Ordering guaranteed WITHIN a partition only
• No global ordering across partitions
• Use same key for events that must be ordered (same partition)
• max.in.flight.requests.per.connection=1 for strict ordering with retries
20 Kafka vs RabbitMQ vs SQS? Kafka, compare • Kafka: high throughput, log-based, ordered, replay capability
• RabbitMQ: traditional message broker, routing, acknowledgments
• SQS: managed AWS queue, simple, no ordering guarantee
• Kafka for: event streaming, data integration; RabbitMQ for: microservices messaging

Apache Kafka — Interview Questions (Part 2)¶

# Question Keywords Answer
21 How to handle backpressure in Kafka consumers? Backpressure • Increase number of consumers in group
• Increase number of partitions (more parallelism)
• Batch processing: max.poll.records to control batch size
• Monitor consumer lag and auto-scale consumers
22 Kafka security features? Security, SSL • Encryption: SSL/TLS for in-transit data
• Authentication: SASL (PLAIN, SCRAM, GSSAPI/Kerberos)
• Authorization: ACLs for topic/group/cluster permissions
• Encryption at rest: handled by cloud/OS level
23 Idempotent producer — what is it? Idempotent, producer • Ensures exactly-once delivery from producer to broker
• Enable: enable.idempotence=true
• Uses producer ID + sequence number to dedup retries
• No extra cost; should be default for production
24 Kafka transactions? Transaction, atomic • Atomic writes across multiple partitions/topics
• Used with read-process-write pattern
• isolation.level=read_committed for consumers
• Enables exactly-once stream processing end-to-end
25 Dead letter queue (DLQ) pattern in Kafka? DLQ, error handling • Route failed/poison messages to separate topic
• Consumer processes normally; failures go to DLQ topic
• DLQ monitored separately for manual review
• Common in Kafka Connect and Kafka Streams
26 How to increase throughput in Kafka? Throughput, tuning • Increase partitions (more consumer parallelism)
• Producer batching: batch.size, linger.ms
• Compression: compression.type=lz4 (reduces network/disk)
• Increase broker disk I/O capacity
27 Kafka message format and headers? Message, format • Key: optional (for partitioning), bytes
• Value: message payload, bytes
• Headers: metadata key-value pairs (tracing, routing)
• Timestamp: event time or ingestion time
28 Consumer rebalancing — what triggers it? Rebalance, trigger • Consumer joins or leaves the group
• New partitions added to topic
• Consumer fails to send heartbeat within timeout
• Rebalance pauses consumption until partitions reassigned
29 Cooperative vs eager rebalancing? Rebalance, cooperative • Eager: revoke ALL partitions, reassign (stop-the-world)
• Cooperative: only reassign moved partitions (incremental)
• Cooperative reduces downtime during rebalancing
• Cooperative preferred: partition.assignment.strategy=CooperativeStickyAssignor
30 Kafka MirrorMaker — cross-cluster replication? MirrorMaker, DC • Replicates topics between Kafka clusters (multi-DC)
• MirrorMaker 2 (MM2): based on Kafka Connect framework
• Use for: disaster recovery, geographic distribution
• Preserves offsets and consumer group state
31 How to design Kafka topics? Design, topic • One topic per event type (orders, clicks, logs)
• Choose appropriate number of partitions (scale later is hard)
• Key design: determines partition placement and ordering
• Retention policy matches use case (real-time vs audit)
32 Exactly-once end-to-end with Kafka? Exactly-once, E2E • Producer: idempotent (enable.idempotence=true)
• Consumer: read_committed isolation level
• Processing: Kafka Streams transactions
• Sink: idempotent writes (upsert/Delta MERGE)
33 Kafka partition reassignment? Reassignment • Redistribute partitions across brokers for balance
• Tool: kafka-reassign-partitions.sh
• Triggered by: adding brokers, uneven load distribution
• Careful: large reassignments impact cluster performance
34 Kafka quotas and throttling? Quotas, throttling • Limit produce/consume rate per client (bytes/sec)
• Prevent noisy clients from overwhelming cluster
• Set per user, per client-id, or both
• Throttled clients receive THROTTLED response
35 CDC (Change Data Capture) with Kafka? CDC, Debezium • Capture row-level changes from databases into Kafka
• Debezium: most popular CDC connector (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB)
• Produces insert/update/delete events as Kafka messages
• Use for: real-time sync, event-driven architectures
36 Kafka on Kubernetes? K8s, Kubernetes • Strimzi: Kubernetes operator for Kafka
• Confluent for Kubernetes: enterprise operator
• Benefits: auto-scaling, self-healing, declarative config
• Challenges: persistent storage, network configuration
37 Confluent Platform — what does it add? Confluent • Enterprise Kafka distribution by original Kafka creators
• Adds: Schema Registry, ksqlDB, Control Center, connectors
• Managed: Confluent Cloud (fully managed Kafka-as-a-Service)
• Extra: enterprise security, multi-tenancy, tiered storage
38 Kafka on cloud — managed services? Cloud, managed • Confluent Cloud: fully managed, multi-cloud
• AWS MSK: managed Kafka on AWS
• Azure Event Hubs: Kafka-compatible managed service
• Google Pub/Sub: not Kafka but similar pub/sub pattern
39 When NOT to use Kafka? Anti-pattern, don't use • Simple request-response (use REST APIs instead)
• Small data volumes (overhead not justified)
• Strict transaction ordering across topics (complex)
• Better alternatives: RabbitMQ for task queues; SQS for simple queuing
40 Kafka performance tuning checklist? Tuning, checklist • Producer: batch.size, linger.ms, compression, acks
• Consumer: fetch.min.bytes, max.poll.records, partition count
• Broker: num.io.threads, log.flush.interval, replication factor
• Monitor: consumer lag, disk I/O, network throughput

Part 12: Apache Airflow¶

Overview¶

Apache Airflow is a workflow orchestration platform for scheduling, monitoring, and managing data pipelines as code (DAGs — Directed Acyclic Graphs).

Architecture¶

Source: Apache Airflow Official Documentation

Key Concepts¶

Concept Description
DAG Directed Acyclic Graph — defines task dependencies and execution order
Task Unit of work within a DAG (Python function or operator)
Operator Template for a task (BashOperator, PythonOperator, SparkSubmitOperator)
Sensor Special operator that waits for condition (file exists, time reached)
XCom Cross-communication: pass data between tasks
TaskFlow Pythonic way to define tasks using decorators (Airflow 2+)
Hook Interface to external systems (database, S3, Spark)
Connection Stored credentials for external systems
Variable Global key-value config accessible across DAGs

Executors¶

Executor Description Use Case
Sequential Single process, one task at a time Development only
Local Multi-process, parallel on one machine Small deployments
Celery Distributed workers via Redis/RabbitMQ Production (common)
Kubernetes Each task runs in its own K8s pod Cloud-native, isolation
In [12]:
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Example Airflow DAG (Python syntax - runs in Airflow, not here)
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────

# from airflow import DAG
# from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator
# from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator
# from airflow.sensors.filesystem import FileSensor
# from datetime import datetime, timedelta
#
# default_args = {
#     'owner': 'data_team',
#     'retries': 2,
#     'retry_delay': timedelta(minutes=5),
#     'email_on_failure': True,
# }
#
# with DAG(
#     dag_id='daily_etl_pipeline',
#     default_args=default_args,
#     schedule_interval='@daily',
#     start_date=datetime(2025, 1, 1),
#     catchup=False,
#     tags=['etl', 'production'],
# ) as dag:
#
#     wait_for_data = FileSensor(
#         task_id='wait_for_data',
#         filepath='/data/raw/daily_export.csv',
#         poke_interval=300,  # check every 5 min
#         timeout=3600,       # fail after 1 hour
#     )
#
#     def extract_data(**context):
#         print(f"Extracting data for {context['ds']}")
#         return '/data/processed/extracted.parquet'
#
#     extract = PythonOperator(
#         task_id='extract',
#         python_callable=extract_data,
#     )
#
#     transform = BashOperator(
#         task_id='transform',
#         bash_command='spark-submit /jobs/transform.py --date {{ ds }}',
#     )
#
#     load = BashOperator(
#         task_id='load',
#         bash_command='spark-submit /jobs/load_to_warehouse.py --date {{ ds }}',
#     )
#
#     wait_for_data >> extract >> transform >> load

print('Airflow DAG example (commented — runs in Airflow environment only)')
