Apache Airflow — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is Apache Airflow? Airflow, orchestration • Workflow orchestration platform for data pipelines
• Pipelines defined as code (Python DAGs)
• Schedule, monitor, and manage complex workflows
• Rich UI for visualizing runs, logs, and dependencies
2 What is a DAG? DAG, directed • Directed Acyclic Graph — defines task execution order
• Directed: tasks have clear dependencies (A → B → C)
• Acyclic: no circular dependencies (no loops)
• Each DAG has: schedule, start date, tasks, dependencies
3 Key Airflow components? Components, architecture • Web Server: UI for monitoring and managing DAGs
• Scheduler: triggers tasks based on schedule and dependencies
• Executor: runs tasks (Local, Celery, Kubernetes)
• Metadata DB: stores DAG state, task status, XCom data
4 Operators — types and examples? Operator, types • BashOperator: run shell commands
• PythonOperator: run Python functions
• SparkSubmitOperator: submit Spark jobs
• Sensors: wait for conditions (FileSensor, S3KeySensor)
5 What is a Sensor? How to use? Sensor, wait • Special operator that waits for a condition to be met
• Modes: poke (blocks worker), reschedule (frees worker between checks)
• Examples: FileSensor, S3KeySensor, ExternalTaskSensor
• Use reschedule mode for long waits (saves worker resources)
6 XCom — what and how? XCom, communication • Cross-Communication: pass small data between tasks
• Push: ti.xcom_push(key, value) or return from PythonOperator
• Pull: ti.xcom_pull(task_ids='task_name', key='key')
• Warning: XCom is for metadata only — NOT large datasets
7 TaskFlow API (decorators) — how used? TaskFlow, decorator • Pythonic way to define tasks with @task decorator
• Automatic XCom passing between decorated functions
• Cleaner code: no need for explicit PythonOperator
• Available in Airflow 2.0+
8 Schedule interval — cron and presets? Schedule, cron • Cron expression: '0 2 * * *' (daily at 2 AM)
• Presets: @daily, @hourly, @weekly, @monthly
• None: only triggered manually
• schedule_interval vs timetable (Airflow 2.2+)
9 Catchup — what is it? Catchup, backfill • When catchup=True: Airflow runs all missed DAG intervals
• When catchup=False: only current/latest interval runs
• Backfill command: airflow dags backfill -s start -e end dag_id
• Production default: catchup=False (avoid unexpected mass runs)
10 Executors — CeleryExecutor vs KubernetesExecutor? Executor, compare • CeleryExecutor: distributed workers via message broker (Redis/RabbitMQ)
• KubernetesExecutor: each task runs in own K8s pod (isolated)
• Celery: always-on workers, faster startup
• Kubernetes: dynamic scaling, better resource isolation
11 Hooks and Connections? Hook, connection • Hook: Python class interfacing with external systems (S3, PostgreSQL, Spark)
• Connection: stored credentials (URL, user, password, extras)
• Connections stored in Airflow UI or environment variables
• Hooks use Connections for authenticated access
12 Airflow Variables? Variable, config • Global key-value pairs accessible from any DAG
• Store: Variable.set('key', 'value'); Get: Variable.get('key')
• Use for: configuration, paths, feature flags
• Warning: each .get() = DB query (use Jinja templating instead)
13 How to handle task failures and retries? Failure, retry • retries: number of retry attempts per task
• retry_delay: timedelta between retries
• on_failure_callback: function called on failure
• email_on_failure: send email notification
14 Jinja templating in Airflow? Jinja, templating • Use {{ ds }}, {{ execution_date }}, {{ params.key }} in operators
• Rendered at runtime — access DAG run context
• Available in: BashOperator commands, SQL, parameters
• {{ macros.ds_add(ds, -1) }} for date arithmetic
15 Trigger rules — what are they? Trigger, rule • Control when a task runs based on upstream status
• all_success (default): run if all upstreams succeed
• all_failed: run only if all upstreams fail
• one_success, none_failed, all_done for complex flows
16 Branching in Airflow? Branch, conditional • BranchPythonOperator: return task_id to execute next
• Enables conditional execution paths in DAG
• Skipped branches marked as 'skipped' (not failed)
• Use for: different processing based on data/config
17 Dynamic DAGs — how to create? Dynamic, DAG • Generate DAGs programmatically using Python loops
• One DAG per customer/table/region from config
• Use DAG Factory pattern or YAML-based configuration
• Warning: too many dynamic DAGs → scheduler overhead
18 SLA and alerting in Airflow? SLA, alert • SLA: expected task completion time
• sla=timedelta(hours=2): alert if task takes longer
• Email alerts: sla_miss_callback for custom handling
• Monitor in Airflow UI: Browse → SLA Misses
19 Pools and priority in Airflow? Pool, priority • Pool: limit concurrent task execution (e.g., max 5 DB connections)
• Define pool size; tasks assigned to pools
• Priority weight: higher priority tasks execute first
• Use for: resource-constrained environments
20 Data-aware scheduling (Airflow 2.4+)? Dataset, data-aware • Trigger DAGs based on dataset updates (not just time)
• Producer DAG declares dataset output
• Consumer DAG triggered when dataset is updated
• Event-driven orchestration without polling
21 Airflow vs other orchestrators? Compare, orchestrators • Airflow: mature, Python DAGs, rich UI, large community
• Prefect: modern, dynamic flows, better error handling
• Dagster: asset-aware, type-safe, software engineering focus
• Luigi: simpler but less featured than Airflow
22 Best practices for production Airflow? Best practice • Keep DAG files simple and fast to parse
• Use catchup=False unless backfill needed
• Idempotent tasks: same result on re-run
• Use Connections/Secrets for credentials (never hardcode)
23 SubDAGs vs Task Groups? SubDAG, TaskGroup • SubDAGs: nested DAGs (deprecated — deadlock-prone)
• Task Groups: visual grouping in UI (Airflow 2.0+)
• Task Groups recommended: no separate execution context
• Clean UI organization without SubDAG overhead
24 Airflow on Kubernetes (MWAA, Cloud Composer)? Cloud, managed • AWS MWAA: managed Airflow on AWS
• GCP Cloud Composer: managed Airflow on GCP
• Azure: Airflow via AKS or third-party
• Managed services handle: scaling, updates, infrastructure
25 ExternalTaskSensor — cross-DAG dependencies? External, sensor • Wait for task in another DAG to complete
• ExternalTaskSensor(external_dag_id, external_task_id, execution_date_fn)
• Use for: inter-pipeline dependencies
• Alternative: Dataset triggers (Airflow 2.4+)
26 Airflow CLI — useful commands? CLI, commands • airflow dags list: list all DAGs
• airflow tasks test dag_id task_id date: test single task
• airflow dags trigger dag_id: manual trigger
• airflow dags backfill -s start -e end dag_id: backfill
27 Concurrency settings in Airflow? Concurrency • parallelism: max active tasks across ALL DAGs
• max_active_tasks_per_dag: per-DAG concurrency
• max_active_runs_per_dag: parallel DAG runs
• Pool: limit per-resource concurrency
28 How to test Airflow DAGs? Testing • airflow tasks test dag task date: run single task locally
• Unit tests: import DAG, check structure and dependencies
• Integration tests: run DAG with test data
• CI/CD: validate DAGs parse correctly in pipeline
29 execution_date vs logical_date? Execution date • execution_date (Airflow 1.x): start of the scheduled interval
• logical_date (Airflow 2.2+): renamed for clarity
• Represents which interval the DAG run covers, NOT when it runs
• Example: daily DAG runs at 00:01 for interval 00:00-23:59
30 Logging in Airflow? Logging • Task logs stored per task attempt (viewable in UI)
• Remote logging: S3, GCS, Azure Blob for production
• Custom log handlers for centralized logging (ELK, Splunk)
• logging.getLogger(__name__) in Python tasks
31 Airflow providers — what are they? Providers, packages • Separate packages for external integrations (aws, google, spark)
• Installed independently: pip install apache-airflow-providers-google
• Each provider: operators, hooks, sensors for that service
• Allows selective installation of needed integrations
32 How to pass data between tasks safely? Data, passing • XCom: for small metadata (<48KB recommended)
• External storage: write to S3/ADLS, pass path via XCom
• TaskFlow: automatic XCom via return values
• Never pass large DataFrames via XCom
33 Idempotent tasks — how to implement? Idempotent • Same result on re-run (safe retries/backfills)
• Use execution_date for processing, not current date
• MERGE/upsert instead of INSERT to avoid duplicates
• Overwrite mode for file writes
34 DAG versioning and CI/CD? CI/CD, version • DAG files in Git (version controlled)
• CI/CD pipeline: lint → test → deploy to Airflow
• Test: validate DAG parses, check dependencies
• Deploy: sync DAG folder to Airflow (S3, GCS, or rsync)
35 Deferred operators and async execution? Deferred, async • Deferrable operators: free worker while waiting (Airflow 2.2+)
• Uses triggers: lightweight async processes
• Saves resources: worker released during long waits
• Better than sensors with poke mode for long delays

Part 13: SQL for Big Data¶

Key SQL Concepts for Data Engineers¶

Concept Description Engine Support
Window Functions Calculate over grouped sets without collapsing rows All modern SQL engines
CTEs Common Table Expressions — named subqueries for readability All
MERGE INTO Upsert — insert+update+delete atomically Delta Lake, Snowflake, BigQuery
Predicate Pushdown Push WHERE filters to storage layer Spark, Hive, Presto, Athena
Approximate Functions Fast estimates (approx_count_distinct) Spark, BigQuery, Presto
QUALIFY Filter after window function (like HAVING for windows) Snowflake, BigQuery, DuckDB
LATERAL VIEW Explode arrays/maps into rows (Hive/Spark) Hive, Spark
Hints Direct query optimizer (/*+ BROADCAST(t) */) Spark, Hive

SQL for Big Data — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Window functions — ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK? Window, rank • ROW_NUMBER: unique sequential (1,2,3,4)
• RANK: ties get same rank, gaps after (1,2,2,4)
• DENSE_RANK: ties same rank, no gaps (1,2,2,3)
• All use: OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...)
2 Running totals with window functions? Running total • SUM(amount) OVER (ORDER BY date ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING)
• Calculates cumulative sum up to current row
• PARTITION BY for per-group running totals
• RANGE vs ROWS: RANGE considers value ties, ROWS counts positions
3 LAG and LEAD — use cases? LAG, LEAD • LAG(col, n): value from n rows before (previous day sales)
• LEAD(col, n): value from n rows after (next day prediction)
• Use for: change calculation, trend analysis, gap detection
• Requires ORDER BY in window specification
4 CTEs — why and when? CTE, readability • Named subquery using WITH clause for readability
• WITH cte AS (SELECT ...) SELECT * FROM cte
• Better than nested subqueries for complex queries
• Note: in Spark, CTEs may be re-evaluated (not materialized)
5 MERGE INTO — how does it work? MERGE, upsert • Single statement for insert + update + delete based on conditions
• MERGE INTO target USING source ON condition WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT
• Enables CDC/SCD processing in one atomic operation
• Supported in Delta Lake, Snowflake, BigQuery
6 Predicate pushdown — why important? Pushdown, filter • Push WHERE filters to storage/data source layer
• Storage reads only matching data (skip irrelevant)
• Parquet/ORC: skip entire row groups using column stats
• Reduces I/O dramatically for selective queries
7 Column pruning vs predicate pushdown? Pruning, pushdown • Column pruning: read only needed columns
• Predicate pushdown: read only matching rows
• Both reduce I/O; Catalyst applies both automatically
• Columnar formats (Parquet/ORC) benefit most
8 QUALIFY clause — what is it? QUALIFY, window • Filter rows after window function calculation
• SELECT *, RANK() OVER (...) as r FROM t QUALIFY r = 1
• Replaces: subquery wrapping with WHERE on window result
• Supported in: Snowflake, BigQuery, DuckDB; not in Spark
9 Approximate functions — when to use? Approximate, count • approx_count_distinct: fast cardinality estimate (HyperLogLog)
• approx_percentile: approximate quantiles
• Use when: exact result not needed, speed matters
• Much faster than COUNT(DISTINCT) on large datasets
10 GROUP BY with ROLLUP, CUBE, GROUPING SETS? ROLLUP, CUBE • ROLLUP: hierarchical subtotals (region→country→total)
• CUBE: all possible combinations of group-by columns
• GROUPING SETS: specific combinations only
• Avoid multiple union queries for different aggregation levels
11 EXPLAIN plan — how to read? EXPLAIN, plan • Shows query execution steps (scans, joins, shuffles)
• Look for: Scan (data read), Exchange (shuffle), BroadcastHashJoin vs SortMergeJoin
• Cost estimates help identify bottlenecks
• Spark: df.explain(True) shows all optimization stages
12 INNER vs LEFT vs FULL OUTER join — when each? Join, compare • INNER: only matching rows (skip non-matches)
• LEFT: all left rows + matching right (null for no match)
• FULL OUTER: all rows from both sides
• INNER for strict matches; LEFT for keeping all primary records
13 Self join — use cases? Self join • Join a table with itself (different aliases)
• Use for: hierarchical data (manager→employee), comparing rows
• Example: find employees earning more than their manager
• Window functions often replace self-joins
14 Correlated vs non-correlated subquery? Subquery • Non-correlated: independent, runs once
• Correlated: references outer query, runs per row (slow)
• Avoid correlated in big data — use joins or window functions
• EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM t2 WHERE t2.id = t1.id) is correlated
15 Views vs CTEs vs temp tables for complex queries? View, CTE, temp • View: stored query definition, reusable across queries
• CTE: named subquery within one query (readability)
• Temp table: materialized, reusable within session
• Materialized view: precomputed and cached
16 Partitioned vs non-partitioned queries? Query, partition • Partitioned: query engine only scans relevant partitions
• Non-partitioned: full table scan (expensive)
• Always include partition column in WHERE clause
• Partition pruning saves cost and time
17 How to find duplicates in SQL? Duplicate, detect • SELECT col, COUNT(*) FROM t GROUP BY col HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
• Window: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dup_cols ORDER BY id) as rn then rn > 1
• Window approach allows keeping the first/latest record
• Important for data quality in ETL pipelines
18 UNION vs UNION ALL? UNION, ALL • UNION: combines + removes duplicates (expensive — sorts)
• UNION ALL: combines without dedup (faster)
• Always use UNION ALL unless dedup needed
• UNION ALL avoids unnecessary shuffle
19 Handling NULLs in SQL aggregations? NULL, aggregate • COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(col) skips NULLs
• SUM/AVG skip NULLs (don't treat as 0)
• COALESCE(col, 0): replace NULL with default
• NULL comparisons: use IS NULL, not = NULL
20 PIVOT and UNPIVOT in SQL? PIVOT, reshape • PIVOT: rows to columns (year values → column headers)
• UNPIVOT: columns to rows (column headers → row values)
• Spark: groupBy().pivot('col').agg()
• UNPIVOT: use stack() function or Spark 3.4+ UNPIVOT
21 Semi join and anti join? Semi, anti • Semi join: return left rows that have match in right (no right columns)
• Anti join: return left rows WITHOUT match in right
• Semi = faster EXISTS; anti = faster NOT EXISTS
• df.join(other, key, 'left_semi') / 'left_anti'
22 SQL hints in Spark? Hints, optimizer • /*+ BROADCAST(small_table) */ for broadcast join
• /*+ REPARTITION(10, col) */ for repartitioning
• /*+ COALESCE(1) */ for reducing partitions
• Override Catalyst when you know data better
23 TABLESAMPLE — sampling in SQL? Sample • SELECT * FROM table TABLESAMPLE (10 PERCENT)
• Fast exploration on large datasets
• Block-level sampling (not true random per row)
• Use for: development, testing, EDA
24 Date/time functions in Big Data SQL? Date, time • date_trunc('month', col): truncate to month
• datediff(end, start): days between dates
• date_format(col, 'yyyy-MM'): format as string
• Supported in: Spark SQL, Hive, Presto, BigQuery
25 How to optimize SQL queries in Spark? Optimize, SQL • Filter early (reduce data before joins)
• Use broadcast hints for small tables
• Avoid SELECT * (column pruning)
• Partition on frequently filtered columns
26 Recursive CTEs — supported in Big Data? Recursive, CTE • Traditional SQL supports recursive CTEs (hierarchy traversal)
• Spark SQL added support in Spark 3.4+
• Hive: limited support via stored procedures
• Alternative: use GraphFrames or iterative Python logic
27 CTAS vs CVAS — create tables from queries? CTAS • CTAS: CREATE TABLE new AS SELECT ... (create table from query)
• CVAS: CREATE VIEW AS SELECT ... (create view from query)
• CTAS materializes data; CVAS is virtual
• CTAS useful for derived tables in ETL
28 JSON functions in SQL? JSON, SQL • from_json(): parse JSON string to struct
• get_json_object(): extract value by path
• json_tuple(): extract multiple values at once
• to_json(): convert struct/map to JSON string
29 Array functions in SQL? Array, functions • array_contains(arr, val): check if value exists
• size(arr): number of elements
• explode(arr): one row per element
• array_distinct(), array_union(), array_intersect()
30 DISTRIBUTE BY, SORT BY, CLUSTER BY in Hive/Spark? Distribute, sort • DISTRIBUTE BY: control row distribution to reducers (by key)
• SORT BY: sort within each reducer (partial sort)
• CLUSTER BY: DISTRIBUTE BY + SORT BY on same column
• ORDER BY: global sort (single reducer — use carefully)

Part 14: Data Warehousing & Cloud Platforms¶

Dimensional Modeling¶

Schema Structure Best For
Star Fact table + denormalized dimension tables Simple queries, fast joins, BI tools
Snowflake Fact table + normalized dimension tables Storage-efficient, complex dimensions
Data Vault Hub + Link + Satellite tables Auditability, incremental loads, agile

Cloud Data Warehouse Comparison¶

Feature Redshift Snowflake BigQuery Synapse
Cloud AWS Multi-cloud GCP Azure
Architecture Cluster-based Shared storage, separate compute Serverless Dedicated/Serverless
Scaling Manual resize Auto-scale warehouses Auto-scale Manual/Auto
Pricing Per-node Per-second compute Per-query (on-demand) Per-DWU
Concurrency Moderate Excellent (multi-cluster) Excellent (slots) Good
Semi-structured LIMITED (Spectrum) VARIANT type (native JSON) STRUCT/ARRAY native LIMITED

Data Warehousing — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Star schema vs snowflake schema? Star, snowflake • Star: fact table + denormalized dimensions (fast queries, simple joins)
• Snowflake: fact table + normalized dimensions (less redundancy, more joins)
• Star preferred for analytics/BI (simpler SQL)
• Snowflake for storage efficiency and complex dimension hierarchies
2 Fact table vs dimension table? Fact, dimension • Fact: contains business measures/metrics (revenue, quantity, clicks)
• Dimension: descriptive attributes (customer name, product category, date)
• Fact tables are large (millions/billions of rows)
• Dimension tables are smaller (thousands of rows)
3 Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD) — types? SCD, type • SCD Type 1: overwrite old value (no history)
• SCD Type 2: add new row with version/date range (full history)
• SCD Type 3: add column for old/new value (limited history)
• Type 2 most common in data warehousing
4 What are surrogate keys? Why use them? Surrogate, key • System-generated keys (auto-increment, UUID) unrelated to business
• Decouple warehouse from source system keys
• Handle: key changes, multiple sources, SCD Type 2 versioning
• Natural key: business-meaningful (SSN); surrogate: warehouse-internal
5 What is a data mart? Data mart • Subset of data warehouse focused on specific department/function
• Finance mart, marketing mart, sales mart
• Faster queries (less data, simpler schema)
• Fed from central warehouse (dependent) or directly from sources
6 Amazon Redshift — key features? Redshift, AWS • Columnar storage, MPP architecture, petabyte-scale
• Redshift Spectrum: query S3 data without loading
• RA3 nodes: separate compute and storage
• COPY command for fast bulk loading from S3
7 Snowflake — key features? Snowflake • Shared storage + separate compute (multi-cluster warehouses)
• VARIANT type for native semi-structured data (JSON)
• Zero-copy cloning: instant table/schema/database clones
• Time travel: query/restore previous data states
8 BigQuery — key features? BigQuery, GCP • Serverless — no infrastructure to manage
• Pay per query (on-demand) or flat-rate
• Native support for STRUCT, ARRAY, GEOGRAPHY types
• BigQuery ML: train ML models directly in SQL
9 Azure Synapse — key features? Synapse, Azure • Unified analytics: SQL + Spark + data integration
• Dedicated SQL pools (provisioned) or serverless
• Native integration with ADLS Gen2, Power BI
• PolyBase for querying external data
10 What is dbt (Data Build Tool)? dbt, transform • SQL-first transformation tool for analytics engineering
• Models defined as SELECT statements (version controlled)
• Built-in: testing, documentation, lineage
• dbt Core (open-source) or dbt Cloud (managed)
11 dbt models, tests, and documentation? dbt, models • Models: SQL SELECT statements that create tables/views
• Tests: unique, not_null, accepted_values, relationships
• Docs: auto-generated from YAML and SQL comments
• Lineage: visualize data flow across models
12 OLAP cube vs modern analytics? OLAP, cube • Traditional OLAP: precomputed multidimensional aggregations
• Modern: columnar warehouses + BI tools compute on-the-fly
• OLAP cubes largely replaced by Snowflake/BigQuery
• Still relevant concept for understanding aggregation patterns
13 Data Vault modeling? Data Vault • Hub: business keys (customer_id, product_id)
• Link: relationships between hubs (orders link customer+product)
• Satellite: descriptive attributes with history
• Great for: auditability, incremental loads, agile data warehousing
14 ETL vs ELT in cloud warehousing? ETL, ELT, cloud • ELT dominant in cloud: load raw → transform in warehouse
• Cloud warehouses have cheap compute for transformation
• Tools: dbt (transform), Fivetran (load), Spark (transform)
• ETL still used for: data quality before loading
15 Materialized views in warehouses? Materialized, view • Precomputed query results stored physically
• Auto-refreshed on base data changes
• Faster reads for repeated aggregation queries
• Supported in: Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks
16 Data warehouse vs data lakehouse? Warehouse, lakehouse • Warehouse: structured data, SQL-only, schema-on-write
• Lakehouse: all data, ACID + SQL + ML, schema-on-read + write
• Lakehouse replaces separate lake+warehouse
• Warehouse for: pure SQL BI; Lakehouse for: unified analytics
17 Trino (formerly PrestoSQL) — what is it? Trino, Presto • Distributed SQL query engine for multiple data sources
• Query: S3, HDFS, PostgreSQL, MySQL, Kafka from one engine
• No storage — pure compute/query layer
• Fast interactive queries on data lakes
18 Partitioning strategies in warehouses? Partition, strategy • Date partitioning: most common (year/month/day)
• Hash partitioning: even distribution by key
• Range partitioning: ordered ranges (IDs, dates)
• Choose based on: query patterns, data distribution
19 Cluster keys in Snowflake? Cluster key • Defines how data is organized within micro-partitions
• Similar to ZORDER in Databricks
• Improves query pruning for large tables
• Auto-clustering: Snowflake maintains clustering automatically
20 What is query federation? Federation • Query data across multiple systems from single engine
• Trino, Spark (multi-source), Redshift Spectrum
• Avoids ETL for cross-system analytics
• Trade-off: potentially slower than local queries
21 Columnar compression in warehouses? Compression, columnar • Same type values stored together → high compression ratio
• Run-length, dictionary, delta encoding
• Snappy: fast; ZSTD: high ratio (configurable)
• Reduces storage costs and I/O
22 Warehouse cost optimization? Cost, optimize • Partition pruning: query only needed partitions
• Materialized views for repeated queries
• Auto-suspend idle compute (Snowflake warehouses)
• On-demand pricing for variable workloads
23 What is a data catalog in warehousing? Catalog, discovery • Searchable inventory of all datasets and metadata
• Tools: DataHub, Amundsen, Purview, Glue Catalog
• Enables data discovery across organization
• Auto-crawl schemas, tag PII, document tables
24 Reverse ETL — what is it? Reverse ETL • Push data FROM warehouse TO operational systems (CRM, marketing tools)
• Warehouse as source of truth → sync to SaaS apps
• Tools: Census, Hightouch, Rudderstack
• Enables: data-driven operations directly from analytics
25 Zero-copy cloning in Snowflake? Clone, Snowflake • Instant clone of table/schema/database with no data duplication
• Uses metadata pointers (copy-on-write)
• Use for: development/testing copies, branching
• No additional storage cost until data modified
26 External tables in cloud warehouses? External, table • Query data in cloud storage without loading into warehouse
• Redshift Spectrum, BigQuery external tables, Synapse PolyBase
• Schema-on-read for raw data exploration
• Slower than native tables but flexible
27 MPP vs SMP architecture? MPP, SMP • MPP (Massive Parallel Processing): distribute across many nodes
• SMP (Symmetric Multiprocessing): single machine, multiple cores
• MPP: Redshift, BigQuery, Snowflake (scales to PBs)
• SMP: PostgreSQL, MySQL (limited to single machine)
28 What is Kimball vs Inmon methodology? Kimball, Inmon • Kimball: bottom-up, build data marts first, star schemas
• Inmon: top-down, build enterprise DW first, 3NF
• Kimball: faster delivery, business-focused
• Inmon: more rigorous, enterprise-wide consistency
29 Concurrency scaling in Snowflake? Concurrency, Snowflake • Auto-adds compute clusters during peak demand
• Users always get consistent performance
• No configuration needed (transparent)
• First 24 credits/day free
30 What is Activity Schema modeling? Activity, schema • Modern alternative to star schema for event data
• Single fact table: entity, activity, timestamp, features
• Simplifies complex event-driven analytics
• Works well with: dbt, modern cloud warehouses

Part 15: Data Pipeline Design & Orchestration¶

Pipeline Design Principles¶

Principle Description
Idempotency Re-running produces same result (no duplicates)
Reproducibility Same input → same output every time
Observability Monitor, log, alert on pipeline health
Data Quality Validate data at each stage
Fault Tolerance Handle failures gracefully (retries, DLQ)
Data Contracts Agreement between producers and consumers on schema/SLA

Pipeline Design — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is CDC (Change Data Capture)? CDC, capture • Capture row-level changes (insert/update/delete) from source databases
• Tools: Debezium (Kafka-based), AWS DMS, Oracle GoldenGate
• Enables real-time data replication to data lake/warehouse
• Avoids full-table extracts — only changes are propagated
2 How to implement idempotent pipelines? Idempotent • Use MERGE/upsert instead of INSERT to avoid duplicates
• Use execution_date, not current timestamp
• Overwrite mode for file writes
• Test by re-running — same result should occur
3 Data quality frameworks? Quality, framework • Great Expectations: Python-based data validation
• Soda: simple data quality checks via YAML
• dbt tests: built-in data testing (unique, not_null, relationships)
• Deequ (by Amazon): data quality on Spark
4 What are data contracts? Contract, schema • Formal agreement between data producer and consumer
• Specifies: schema, data types, SLAs, freshness, quality rules
• Prevents breaking changes from upstream
• Enforced via schema registry, CI/CD pipeline checks
5 Data observability pillars? Observability • Freshness: is data arriving on time?
• Volume: is the expected amount of data present?
• Schema: have column types/names changed unexpectedly?
• Distribution: are value distributions normal?
• Lineage: where did data come from, what transformed it?
6 Backfilling strategies? Backfill, strategy • Re-process historical data when pipeline logic changes
• Idempotent design: safe to re-run any date range
• Airflow: catchup=True or backfill command
• Partition-based: overwrite specific partitions only
7 Dead letter queue (DLQ) pattern? DLQ, error • Route failed/unparseable messages to separate queue
• Main pipeline continues processing valid data
• DLQ reviewed manually or by automated retry pipeline
• Prevents single bad record from blocking entire pipeline
8 CI/CD for data pipelines? CI/CD, pipeline • Version control: DAGs, SQL, config in Git
• CI: lint, test, validate schemas, dry-run pipelines
• CD: deploy DAGs/code to staging → production
• Tools: GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Azure DevOps
9 Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD) implementation? SCD, implement • SCD Type 1: UPDATE dim SET name = new_name WHERE id = x
• SCD Type 2: INSERT new row, set end_date on old row
• SCD Type 2 with Delta MERGE: match on key, insert new version
• Use surrogate keys for SCD Type 2 versioning
10 ELT pipeline components? ELT, components • Extract: Fivetran, Airbyte, custom connectors
• Load: direct load to cloud storage or warehouse
• Transform: dbt, Spark SQL, warehouse SQL
• Orchestrate: Airflow, Prefect, Dagster
11 How to handle late-arriving data? Late data • Watermarks (Spark Streaming): define acceptable lateness
• Reprocessing: re-run pipeline for affected date range
• MERGE: upsert late records into existing tables
• Grace period: keep partitions open for late arrivals
12 Data pipeline testing strategies? Testing, strategy • Unit tests: validate individual transform functions
• Integration tests: run pipeline with test data
• Data quality tests: assertions on output (count, nulls, ranges)
• Regression tests: compare output against known baseline
13 Schema evolution in pipelines? Schema, evolution • Backward compatible: add columns with defaults
• Schema registry: validate changes before deployment
• Delta Lake: mergeSchema=true for controlled evolution
• Breaking changes: coordinate with consumers via data contracts
14 Micro-batch vs real-time pipeline — tradeoffs? Micro-batch, real-time • Micro-batch: simpler, easier debugging, higher latency (seconds-minutes)
• Real-time: complex, harder to debug, lowest latency (ms)
• Most use cases: micro-batch is sufficient
• Real-time for: fraud detection, live dashboards, trading
15 What is a feature store? Feature, store • Centralized repository for ML features
• Ensures consistency between training and serving
• Tools: Feast, Databricks Feature Store, Hopsworks
• Handles: feature versioning, point-in-time lookups
16 Metadata-driven pipelines? Metadata, driven • Pipeline behavior driven by configuration, not hardcoded logic
• Config: source/target definitions, column mappings, schedules
• Benefits: reusable pipeline code, easy to add new sources
• Implement with: Airflow Variables, YAML config, database tables
17 Event-driven vs schedule-driven orchestration? Event, schedule • Schedule-driven: run at fixed intervals (cron)
• Event-driven: trigger on data arrival, file upload, API call
• Event-driven: lower latency, more efficient
• Airflow 2.4+ supports dataset-aware scheduling
18 What is data deduplication? Strategies? Dedup, strategy • Exact dedup: GROUP BY + ROW_NUMBER (keep first/latest)
• Fuzzy dedup: similarity matching (edit distance, soundex)
• Stream dedup: dropDuplicates with watermark
• Delta MERGE: upsert semantics prevent duplicates
19 Pipeline monitoring and alerting? Monitor, alert • Monitor: row counts, latency, error rates, data freshness
• Alert channels: email, Slack, PagerDuty
• Dashboards: Grafana, Datadog, CloudWatch
• SLA monitoring in Airflow
20 Cost management for data pipelines? Cost, manage • Right-size compute: auto-scaling, spot instances
• Partition pruning: avoid full table scans
• Data lifecycle: archive/delete old data
• Monitoring: track cost per pipeline/team
21 What is DataOps? DataOps • Agile methodology for data pipeline development and operations
• Combines: DevOps + data engineering practices
• Pillars: automation, testing, monitoring, collaboration
• Goal: faster, more reliable data delivery
22 How to version data? Data, versioning • Delta Lake time travel: VERSION AS OF
• DVC (Data Version Control): Git-like for data/models
• LakeFS: Git-like branching for data lakes
• Enables: reproducibility, auditability, rollback
23 Access patterns for pipeline design? Access, patterns • Write-heavy: streaming ingestion (append-only, STCS compaction)
• Read-heavy: aggregation tables (pre-computed, materialized views)
• Mixed: separate read/write layers (CQRS pattern)
• Design pipelines around dominant access pattern
24 What is a data mesh? Data mesh • Decentralized data architecture: domain teams own their data
• Principles: domain ownership, data as product, self-service, governance
• Alternative to centralized data team model
• Each domain publishes discoverable data products
25 What is a data fabric? Data fabric • AI-driven data management across distributed environments
• Auto-discovers, catalogs, and integrates data assets
• Works across: on-prem, multi-cloud, hybrid
• Different from mesh: fabric is technology-driven, mesh is organizational

Part 16: Performance Tuning & Optimization¶

Spark Performance Tuning Checklist¶

Area Check Action
Shuffle Too many shuffle partitions? Tune spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (default 200)
Skew Straggler tasks? Salting, AQE, broadcast join
Join Large shuffle reads? Broadcast small tables
Cache Recomputing same data? cache()/persist() reused DataFrames
UDF Slow Python UDFs? Replace with built-in functions or Pandas UDFs
Serialization High serialization time? Use Kryo serialization
GC High GC time? Tune memory, reduce object creation
Files Too many small files? OPTIMIZE/coalesce, avoid too many partitions

Performance Tuning — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 How to identify bottlenecks in Spark UI? Spark UI, bottleneck • Stages tab: check for skewed tasks (one task much longer)
• Shuffle read/write: high values indicate expensive shuffles
• GC time: high GC in Executors tab = memory pressure
• Task duration distribution: look for stragglers
2 Data skew — how to detect and fix? Skew, detect • Detect: Spark UI shows one partition much larger; task times vary 10x+
• Fix: salting (random prefix on key), AQE (auto-splits skewed partitions)
• Fix: broadcast join for small-large table joins
• Fix: repartition with different key
3 Salting technique — step by step? Salting, steps • Add random salt (0 to N) as prefix to skewed key: concat(rand_int, '-', key)
• Explode other table with same salt range (cross join with salt)
• Join on salted key → distributes evenly
• After join: remove salt prefix, re-aggregate if needed
4 Spark shuffle partitions — how to tune? Shuffle, partitions • Default: 200 (spark.sql.shuffle.partitions)
• Too few: large partitions → OOM or slow tasks
• Too many: overhead per small partition
• Rule: target ~128 MB per partition; AQE auto-coalesces
5 Broadcast join threshold? Broadcast, threshold • Default: 10 MB (spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold)
• Increase for larger lookup tables: .config('...', '100m')
• Manual hint: F.broadcast(df)
• AQE can auto-switch to broadcast at runtime
6 When to use cache/persist? When is it harmful? Cache, harmful • Good: DataFrame reused multiple times in same job
• Bad: single-use DataFrame (wastes memory, causes eviction)
• Bad: very large DataFrame (spills to disk, slow)
• Always unpersist after use
7 UDF performance — why slow with Python UDFs? UDF, slow • Data serialized from JVM to Python and back (per row)
• Breaks Catalyst optimization (black box)
• Fix: use built-in functions whenever possible
• Fix: Pandas UDFs (vectorized, Apache Arrow, 10-100x faster)
8 Kryo serialization — when and why? Kryo, serialization • Kryo is 10x faster and more compact than Java serialization
• Enable: spark.serializer=org.apache.spark.serializer.KryoSerializer
• Register custom classes for best performance
• Used for: shuffle data, cache serialization
9 Small files problem in Spark? Small files, compact • Too many small files → excessive metadata, slow reads
• Caused by: many partitions, streaming micro-batches
• Fix: coalesce(n) before write, OPTIMIZE (Delta)
• Target: 128-256 MB per file
10 Executor memory tuning? Executor, memory • spark.executor.memory: heap size (try 8-16g per executor)
• spark.executor.memoryOverhead: 10% + additional for off-heap
• spark.memory.fraction: 0.6 default (execution+storage)
• Balance: fewer large executors vs. many small executors
11 Number of executors vs cores per executor? Executors, cores • Cores per executor: 4-5 recommended (HDFS I/O degrades above 5)
• Too many cores: contention; too few: under-utilization
• Total cores = executors × cores_per_executor
• Leave 1 core per node for OS/YARN
12 How to reduce GC overhead? GC, overhead • Reduce long-lived object creation (avoid collect on large data)
• Use off-heap storage (Tungsten, persist with DISK_ONLY)
• Tune G1GC: -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=35
• Monitor GC time in Executors tab of Spark UI
13 Dynamic allocation benefits and config? Dynamic, allocation • Auto-scale executors based on workload
• spark.dynamicAllocation.enabled=true
• Requires: external shuffle service
• Saves cost when workload varies (scale down when idle)
14 Partition pruning — how to leverage? Partition, pruning • Query must include partition column in WHERE clause
• Spark skips reading entire partitions that don't match
• Write data partitioned by frequently filtered columns
• Check: explain() should show PartitionFilters
15 How to minimize shuffle in joins? Shuffle, minimize • Broadcast join: avoid shuffle entirely for small tables
• Co-partition: repartition both tables on join key before join
• Bucketing: pre-hash both tables by join key
• AQE: automatic optimization at runtime
16 Explain plan — what to look for? Explain, optimize • BroadcastHashJoin: good (no shuffle)
• SortMergeJoin: shuffle both sides (expensive)
• WholeStageCodegen: Tungsten optimization active (good)
• Filter pushdown: filters appear early in plan
17 File format impact on performance? Format, performance • Parquet/ORC: columnar, compressed, predicate pushdown (fast)
• CSV/JSON: row-based, no columnar optimization (slow)
• Always convert raw CSV/JSON to Parquet/Delta for analytics
• Delta: adds ACID + data skipping on top of Parquet
18 How to handle OOM errors? OOM, memory • Increase executor memory or number of executors
• Repartition to create more/smaller partitions
• Avoid collect() on large datasets (bring to driver)
• Reduce broadcast variables if too large for executors
19 spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes? MaxPartition, bytes • Max bytes per partition when reading files (default 128 MB)
• Decrease for: narrow tables (more parallelism)
• Increase for: wide tables (reduce task overhead)
• Balance: too small = too many tasks; too large = OOM
20 What is data locality in Spark? Data locality • Process data on the node where it resides
• Levels: PROCESS_LOCAL → NODE_LOCAL → RACK_LOCAL → ANY
• Spark prefers local but may schedule remotely under pressure
• Locality mostly relevant for HDFS; less for cloud storage
21 How to profile Spark jobs? Profile, metrics • Spark UI: stages, tasks, shuffle, cache metrics
• Event log: spark.eventLog.enabled=true
• Spark History Server: analyze completed jobs
• Metrics: Prometheus/Graphite sink for monitoring
22 Cost vs performance tradeoffs? Cost, performance • More executors = faster but more expensive
• Spot/preemptible instances: 60-90% cheaper, risk of interruption
• Cache frequently used data (saves recomputation cost)
• Optimize file format and partitioning before scaling hardware
23 Tungsten off-heap memory? Tungsten, off-heap • Stores data outside JVM heap (avoids GC overhead)
• Managed by Spark directly (not JVM garbage collector)
• Enable via: spark.memory.offHeap.enabled=true
• Useful for: large memory workloads, reducing GC pauses
24 How AQE improves performance automatically? AQE, automatic • Coalesce shuffle partitions: merges small partitions after shuffle
• Dynamic join strategy: switches to broadcast if input is small enough
• Skew join optimization: splits skewed partitions into sub-splits
• All happen at runtime based on real statistics
25 Benchmarking Spark jobs? Benchmark, test • Use same data, same cluster config for fair comparison
• Measure: end-to-end time, shuffle bytes, tasks count
• Compare: before/after optimization changes
• Tools: Spark UI metrics, time.time() in code, spark-measure library

Part 17: AWS Data Engineering¶

AWS Services Matrix¶

Category Service Purpose
Storage S3 Object storage — data lake foundation
Ingestion Kinesis Data Streams Real-time streaming ingestion
Kinesis Firehose Managed delivery to S3/Redshift/ElasticSearch
DMS Database Migration Service (CDC-capable)
AppFlow SaaS data ingestion (Salesforce, SAP)
Processing Glue Serverless ETL (Spark-based)
EMR Managed Spark/Hadoop/Presto clusters
Lambda Serverless functions (event-driven)
Query Athena Serverless SQL on S3 (Presto-based)
Redshift Cloud data warehouse (MPP)
Orchestration Step Functions Visual workflow orchestration
MWAA Managed Apache Airflow
Catalog Glue Catalog Central metadata/schema registry
Lake Formation Data lake governance and access control

AWS Data Engineering — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is Amazon S3? Key features for data engineering? S3, storage • Object storage — unlimited, durable (11 9s), cost-effective
• Storage tiers: Standard, IA, Glacier for lifecycle management
• S3 Events → trigger Lambda/SQS/SNS on object creation
• Foundation for data lakes: store raw, processed, and curated data
2 S3 storage classes — which for what? S3, classes • Standard: frequent access (hot data, active analytics)
• Intelligent-Tiering: auto-moves between tiers
• Infrequent Access: less accessed, lower cost (compliance data)
• Glacier: archive data, minutes-to-hours retrieval
3 What is AWS Glue? Glue, ETL • Serverless ETL service built on Spark (PySpark)
• Auto-discovers schemas with Glue Crawlers
• Glue Studio: visual drag-and-drop ETL pipeline builder
• DPU-based pricing (Data Processing Units)
4 Glue Crawlers — what do they do? Crawler, catalog • Scan data sources and infer schemas automatically
• Populate Glue Data Catalog with table definitions
• Support: S3 (CSV, JSON, Parquet), JDBC databases
• Schedule crawlers to keep catalog up-to-date
5 Glue Catalog — why important? Catalog, metadata • Central metadata repository for all AWS analytics services
• Shared by: Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR, Glue
• Compatible with Hive metastore API
• Stores: table schemas, partitions, statistics
6 What is Amazon Athena? Athena, query • Serverless SQL query engine on S3 data
• Pay per query (per TB scanned)
• Based on Presto/Trino engine
• Best with: Parquet/ORC (columnar → less scan → cheaper)
7 Athena vs Redshift — when each? Athena, Redshift • Athena: ad-hoc queries, serverless, pay per query
• Redshift: heavy analytics, complex joins, persistent warehouse
• Athena for: exploration, occasional queries
• Redshift for: BI dashboards, high-concurrency workloads
8 Amazon Redshift — architecture? Redshift, MPP • Massively Parallel Processing (MPP) columnar warehouse
• Leader node: query coordination; Compute nodes: execute queries
• RA3 nodes: separate compute from storage (S3-backed)
• Distribution: KEY, EVEN, ALL for data distribution
9 Redshift Spectrum — what is it? Spectrum, external • Query S3 data directly from Redshift (without loading)
• Uses Redshift SQL + S3 as external data source
• Parallel processing: Spectrum nodes in S3 layer
• Use for: infrequent queries on cold data in S3
10 Kinesis Data Streams vs Kinesis Firehose? Kinesis, compare • Data Streams: real-time, custom consumer code, manual scaling
• Firehose: managed delivery to S3/Redshift/ES, auto-scaling
• Data Streams: sub-second latency, 7-day retention
• Firehose: at least 60-second buffer, no manual management
11 What is Amazon EMR? EMR, managed • Managed cluster for Spark, Hadoop, Presto, Hive, HBase
• Quick deployment with auto-scaling and spot instances
• EMR on EKS: run Spark on Kubernetes
• EMR Serverless: no cluster management needed
12 AWS Lambda in data pipelines? Lambda, serverless • Serverless functions triggered by events (S3, Kinesis, API)
• Good for: lightweight transforms, file processing, glue between services
• Limitations: 15-min timeout, 10 GB memory, ephemeral
• Use with SQS/SNS for async processing
13 AWS Step Functions for orchestration? Step Functions • Visual workflow orchestrator using state machines
• Chain AWS services: Glue, Lambda, ECS, EMR
• Built-in: error handling, retries, parallel execution
• Alternative to Airflow for AWS-native pipelines
14 AWS Lake Formation? Lake Formation • Managed service for setting up and securing data lakes
• Central permissions: fine-grained access control on S3 data
• Blueprints: automated data ingestion from databases
• Tag-based access control for columns and rows
15 DMS (Database Migration Service)? DMS, migration • Migrate databases to AWS (or between AWS databases)
• Supports CDC: continuous replication of changes
• Full load + ongoing replication
• Targets: S3, RDS, Redshift, DynamoDB
16 S3 partitioning strategy for analytics? S3, partition • /data/year=2024/month=01/day=15/ (Hive-style partitioning)
• Enables partition pruning in Athena/Spark/Glue
• Avoid too many small partitions (small files problem)
• Choose granularity based on query patterns
17 Glue vs EMR — which to choose? Glue, EMR • Glue: serverless, pay per DPU-hour, auto-scaling, simpler
• EMR: full cluster control, more config options, persistent
• Glue for: standard ETL, smaller jobs, quick setup
• EMR for: complex Spark, ML workloads, custom libraries
18 EventBridge in data pipelines? EventBridge, events • Serverless event bus for routing events between services
• Schedule events: cron-like triggers for Glue/Lambda
• Cross-account event routing
• Use for: event-driven pipeline orchestration
19 SQS vs SNS vs Kinesis? SQS, SNS, Kinesis • SQS: message queue (point-to-point, at-least-once delivery)
• SNS: pub/sub notification (fan-out to multiple subscribers)
• Kinesis: streaming data (ordered, replay, real-time analytics)
• SQS for decoupling; SNS for notifications; Kinesis for streaming
20 Redshift COPY command optimization? COPY, Redshift • COPY: fastest bulk load from S3 to Redshift
• Use compressed files (GZIP, LZO, ZSTD)
• Split data into multiple files (parallel COPY)
• Use MANIFEST file for exact file listing
21 Cost optimization on AWS data pipelines? Cost, AWS • Use spot instances on EMR (60-90% savings)
• Athena: use Parquet/ORC (pay per scan — less data = cheaper)
• S3 lifecycle policies: move old data to Glacier
• Glue: right-size DPUs, use Glue bookmarks to avoid reprocessing
22 Glue bookmarks — what are they? Bookmark, Glue • Track previously processed data to avoid reprocessing
• Enable incremental ETL (only new data processed)
• Automatically maintain high-water mark
• Essential for cost savings on recurring jobs
23 AWS data pipeline architecture example? Architecture, example • Ingestion: Kinesis/DMS → S3 Raw (Bronze)
• Processing: Glue Spark → S3 Clean (Silver)
• Analytics: Athena/Redshift → S3 Curated (Gold)
• Orchestration: Step Functions or MWAA (Airflow)
24 DynamoDB for data engineering? DynamoDB • NoSQL key-value and document database (fully managed)
• Single-digit millisecond latency at any scale
• DynamoDB Streams: CDC for triggering Lambda/pipelines
• Use for: operational data, not analytics
25 CloudWatch monitoring for pipelines? CloudWatch • Metrics: Glue job metrics, EMR cluster health, Lambda errors
• Alarms: trigger SNS on metric thresholds
• Logs: centralize pipeline logs for debugging
• Dashboards: visualize pipeline health
26 IAM roles and policies for data access? IAM, security • Role-based access: assign roles to Glue/EMR/Lambda
• Least privilege: minimum permissions needed
• Service-linked roles: Glue service role for S3 access
• Resource policies on S3 buckets for cross-account
27 AWS Glue DataBrew? DataBrew, visual • Visual data preparation tool (no code / low code)
• 250+ built-in transformations
• Profile datasets: data quality, distributions, outliers
• Good for: analysts, quick data exploration
28 Amazon MSK for Kafka? MSK, Kafka • Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (fully managed)
• Deploy, run, scale Kafka clusters without management overhead
• Integrates with: Glue, Lambda, Kinesis Data Analytics
• MSK Serverless: auto-scaling, pay-per-use Kafka
29 QuickSight for BI? QuickSight, BI • AWS-native BI service for dashboards and visualizations
• Connect to: Athena, Redshift, RDS, S3
• ML-powered: anomaly detection, forecasting
• Pay-per-session pricing model
30 AWS Glue Schema Registry? Schema, registry • Manage and enforce schemas for streaming data
• Support: Avro, JSON Schema formats
• Integrate with Kinesis, MSK, Lambda
• Ensure schema compatibility before publishing
31 Cross-account data sharing on AWS? Cross-account • S3 bucket policies + IAM roles for data access
• Lake Formation: cross-account table sharing
• AWS RAM: share Glue Catalog resources
• Redshift: datasharing (read-only across clusters)
32 Data encryption on AWS? Encryption, security • S3: SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, SSE-C (server-side) or client-side
• Redshift: AES-256 encryption for data at rest
• In-transit: TLS/SSL for connections
• KMS: centralized key management
33 VPC Endpoints for data services? VPC, endpoint • Private connectivity to AWS services without internet
• Gateway endpoints: S3, DynamoDB (free)
• Interface endpoints: Glue, Kinesis, other services
• Security: keep data traffic within VPC
34 Redshift vs Athena vs EMR — decision matrix? Decision, compare • Redshift: persistent BI warehouse, complex analytics
• Athena: ad-hoc queries, serverless, pay-per-scan
• EMR: large-scale Spark processing, ML workloads
• Often used together: EMR→S3→Athena/Redshift
35 AWS data engineering certifications? Certification • AWS Certified Data Engineer – Associate
• AWS Certified Database – Specialty
• Covers: S3, Glue, Athena, Redshift, Kinesis, EMR, Lake Formation
• Good for career advancement and validating skills
36 AWS Step Functions for pipelines? Step Functions • Orchestrate multi-step workflows as state machines
• Visual workflow builder; error handling built-in
• Integrates with: Glue, Lambda, ECS, EMR
• Alternative to Airflow for AWS-native orchestration
37 AWS Glue Crawlers? Crawlers, schema • Auto-discover schema from data in S3/RDS/Redshift
• Populate Glue Data Catalog with table definitions
• Schedule: on-demand, periodic, or event-triggered
• Handles schema evolution and new partitions
38 AWS Lake Formation? Lake Formation • Managed data lake: security, governance, ETL in one service
• Fine-grained access: column-level, row-level, tag-based
• Integrates with Glue catalog and IAM
• Cross-account sharing with centralized permissions
39 Amazon MSK (Managed Kafka)? MSK, Kafka • Fully managed Apache Kafka on AWS
• Serverless option: auto-scales, pay-per-data
• Integrates with: Glue, Lambda, Kinesis Data Analytics
• vs Kinesis: MSK is open-source compatible; Kinesis is simpler
40 AWS DynamoDB for DE? DynamoDB • NoSQL key-value store: single-digit ms latency at any scale
• Use in DE: pipeline metadata, lock tables, lookup tables
• Streams: CDC-like event stream of table changes
• On-demand vs provisioned capacity modes
41 AWS Glue Interactive Sessions? Glue, interactive • Serverless Spark environment for development
• Start in seconds (vs minutes for EMR notebooks)
• Pay per second of compute; auto-stop on idle
• Good for: development, debugging, ad-hoc analysis
42 Amazon OpenSearch for log analytics? OpenSearch • Managed Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for search and analytics
• Use case: log analytics, operational dashboards

43 AWS Clean Rooms? Clean Rooms • Collaborate on data without sharing raw data

44 S3 storage classes for data lakes? S3, storage • Standard: frequently accessed (hot data)

45 IAM for data engineering? IAM, security • Roles > users for services (Glue role, EMR role)
