Part 19: Apache Flink¶

Flink Architecture¶

Component Description
JobManager Master: receives jobs, schedules tasks, manages checkpoints
TaskManager Worker: runs tasks in slots (parallel pipelines)
Slot Fixed portion of a TaskManager's resources (CPU + memory)
Checkpoint Consistent snapshot of distributed state for fault tolerance
Savepoint Manual checkpoint — used for upgrades, migration, A/B testing
State Backend Where state is stored: HashMapStateBackend (heap) or EmbeddedRocksDB

Flink vs Spark Streaming¶

Aspect Apache Flink Spark Structured Streaming
Processing True event-at-a-time Micro-batch (or continuous experimental)
Latency Milliseconds Seconds (micro-batch interval)
State First-class managed state State via grouping/aggregation
Exactly-once Native (Chandy-Lamport checkpointing) Via idempotent sinks + checkpoints
Windows Flexible (tumbling, sliding, session, global) Tumbling, sliding, session
Batch Treats batch as bounded stream Native batch mode
Ecosystem Growing Very mature (ML, SQL, Graph)

Apache Flink — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is Apache Flink? Flink, streaming • Distributed stream processing framework
• True event-at-a-time processing (not micro-batch)
• Unified batch + stream processing
• Used at: Alibaba, Uber, Netflix, LinkedIn
2 Flink vs Spark Streaming? Flink, Spark • Flink: true streaming, millisecond latency, native state
• Spark: micro-batch, seconds latency, larger ecosystem
• Flink better for: low-latency, complex event processing
• Spark better for: batch-heavy workloads, ML integration
3 How does Flink achieve exactly-once? Exactly-once • Chandy-Lamport distributed snapshot algorithm
• Barriers injected into data streams
• Aligned checkpoints: wait for all barriers
• Unaligned checkpoints: don't wait (lower latency)
4 Flink state backends? State, backend • HashMapStateBackend: state in JVM heap (fast, limited by memory)
• EmbeddedRocksDBStateBackend: state on disk (larger, slower)
• RocksDB for TB-scale state; HashMap for small fast state
• State is checkpointed to durable storage (S3/HDFS)
5 Window types in Flink? Windows • Tumbling: fixed-size, non-overlapping (e.g., every 5 min)
• Sliding: fixed-size, overlapping (5 min window, 1 min slide)
• Session: gap-based (close after inactivity timeout)
• Global: all elements in one window (custom triggers)
6 Watermarks in Flink? Watermarks • Timestamps indicating "no events earlier than this will arrive"
• Drive event-time window evaluation
• Strategies: periodic (interval-based) or punctuated (special events)
• Late data: side outputs or allowed lateness
7 Checkpoints vs savepoints? Checkpoint, save • Checkpoints: automatic, lightweight, for fault recovery
• Savepoints: manual, full snapshot, for upgrades/migrations
• Checkpoints can be incremental (RocksDB); savepoints are full
• Savepoints survive job changes; checkpoints may not
8 Flink DataStream API? DataStream • Core API for stream processing
• Operations: map, filter, keyBy, window, process
• ProcessFunction: access to timers, state, side outputs
• Supports: event-time, watermarks, checkpointing
9 Flink Table API / SQL? Table, SQL • Declarative API on top of DataStream
• SQL for stream processing (SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY)
• Dynamic tables: continuously updating query results
• Temporal joins for enrichment from slowly changing tables
10 Flink CDC (Change Data Capture)? CDC, Flink • Flink CDC connectors read database changelogs
• Supports: MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Oracle
• No need for separate Debezium + Kafka setup
• Direct database-to-Flink streaming pipeline
11 Backpressure in Flink? Backpressure • Automatic: slow consumer slows down producer (credit-based flow control)
• Monitor: Flink Web UI shows backpressure per operator
• Fix: scale operators, optimize slow functions, adjust parallelism
• Better than Spark's rate-limiting
12 Flink parallelism? Parallelism • Operator-level parallelism: each operator can have different parallelism
• Task slots determine max parallelism per TaskManager
• keyBy redistributes by key hash
• rebalance for round-robin redistribution
13 Event time vs processing time? Event, processing • Event time: when event actually occurred (embedded timestamp)
• Processing time: when event is processed by Flink
• Ingestion time: when event enters Flink
• Event time preferred for correctness; processing time for lower latency
14 Side outputs in Flink? Side output • Produce multiple output streams from single operator
• Use case: late data handling, error routing, splitting streams
• Tagged with OutputTag
• Alternative to filter chains (more efficient)
15 When to choose Flink over Spark? Choose, decision • Sub-second latency requirements (fraud, alerting)
• Complex event processing (patterns, sequences)
• Large managed state (TB-scale keyed state)
• True exactly-once semantics critical
• Session windows with complex triggers
16 Flink deployment modes? Deploy, modes • Session cluster: shared cluster, multiple jobs
• Per-job cluster: isolated cluster per job (deprecated)
• Application mode: dedicated cluster, all jobs in one JAR
• Kubernetes native: Flink Kubernetes Operator
17 Flink async I/O? Async, IO • Enrich stream by async calls to external systems
• Doesn't block processing while waiting for response
• Ordered vs unordered result emission
• Better throughput than synchronous enrichment
18 How does Flink handle late data? Late, data • Watermarks define "too late" threshold
• allowedLateness: update window results for late elements
• Side outputs: collect late data separately for reprocessing
• Trade-off: completeness vs latency
19 Flink memory model? Memory • JVM Heap: for user code objects
• Managed Memory: for state backends, sorting, caching
• Network Memory: for shuffle buffers between operators
• Configure: taskmanager.memory.process.size and sub-components
20 Flink connectors? Connectors • Source: Kafka, Kinesis, JDBC, filesystem, CDC
• Sink: Kafka, JDBC, Elasticsearch, filesystem, Delta Lake
• Exactly-once sinks via two-phase commit protocol
• Custom connectors via Source/Sink API

Part 20: Data Modeling¶

Normalization Forms¶

Form Rule Example Violation
1NF Atomic values, no repeating groups Column with comma-separated values
2NF 1NF + no partial dependencies on composite key Non-key column depends on part of composite key
3NF 2NF + no transitive dependencies Column A → B → C (C depends on A transitively)
BCNF Every determinant is a candidate key Non-candidate key determines another column

Modeling Methodologies¶

Methodology Key Concepts Best For
Kimball Star schema, conformed dimensions, bus matrix Department-level analytics, bottom-up
Inmon Enterprise data warehouse, 3NF, then data marts Enterprise-wide, top-down
Data Vault 2.0 Hubs (business keys), Links (relationships), Satellites (attributes) Agile, auditable, historical DW
Activity Schema Single wide table with activity_id, entity, timestamp, features Event-driven analytics, ML feature engineering
One Big Table Fully denormalized single table Simple analytics, small teams

Data Modeling — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is normalization? Normalization • Organizing data to reduce redundancy and improve integrity
• Progressive forms: 1NF → 2NF → 3NF → BCNF
• Trade-off: less redundancy vs more joins
• OLTP systems typically 3NF; analytics often denormalized
2 Star schema vs snowflake schema? Star, snowflake • Star: denormalized dimensions directly connected to fact table
• Snowflake: normalized dimensions (dimension → sub-dimension)
• Star: simpler queries, faster (fewer joins), more storage
• Snowflake: less storage, more complex queries
3 Fact tables vs dimension tables? Fact, dimension • Fact: measurable events (sales amount, quantity, clicks)
• Dimension: descriptive context (customer, product, date)
• Fact types: transaction, periodic snapshot, accumulating snapshot
• Dimensions: slowly changing (SCD Types 1/2/3)
4 SCD Type 1 vs Type 2? SCD, types • Type 1: overwrite old value (no history, simple)
• Type 2: add new row with start/end dates + is_current flag
• Type 2 implemented with Delta MERGE + surrogate keys
• Type 3: add previous value column (limited history)
5 What is Data Vault 2.0? Data Vault • Hub: unique business keys (customer_id, product_code)
• Link: relationships between hubs (order links customer to product)
• Satellite: descriptive attributes with timestamps
• Benefits: auditable, handles schema changes, parallel loading
6 Surrogate keys vs natural keys? Surrogate, natural • Surrogate: system-generated (auto-increment, UUID)
• Natural: business-meaningful (SSN, email, product_code)
• Surrogate preferred for DW: stable, compact, no business logic
• Natural keys can change, causing cascade updates
7 Conformed dimensions? Conformed • Shared dimensions used consistently across fact tables
• Kimball bus matrix maps dimensions to business processes
• Enables cross-process analysis (same customer dim in sales vs support)
• Requires governance and agreement across teams
8 Degenerate dimensions? Degenerate • Dimension attributes stored in fact table (no separate dim table)
• Example: order_number, invoice_number in fact table
• Used when dimension has no additional attributes
• Reduces joins without losing information
9 Junk dimensions? Junk dimension • Combine low-cardinality flags/indicators into single dimension
• Instead of: is_online, is_mobile, is_premium as separate dims
• Create one junk_dim with all combinations
• Reduces fact table width and number of small dimensions
10 Grain of a fact table? Grain • The level of detail each row represents
• Example: one row per order line item per day
• Must be declared before building fact table
• All facts must be true at the declared grain
11 Normalization vs denormalization trade-offs? Trade-off • Normalized: less redundancy, data integrity, slower queries (joins)
• Denormalized: faster reads, more storage, update anomalies
• OLTP: normalize for write performance
• OLAP: denormalize for read performance
12 Activity Schema? Activity • Single wide table: entity_id, activity, timestamp, feature_1..N
• No joins needed for analytics queries
• Easy for ML feature engineering
• Trade-off: very wide tables, storage overhead
13 When to use Data Vault vs Kimball? Vault, Kimball • Data Vault: enterprise DW, regulatory/audit needs, agile teams
• Kimball: departmental analytics, simpler reporting
• Data Vault: handles source changes better
• Kimball: easier for business users to query directly
14 Accumulating snapshot facts? Accumulating • Track lifecycle milestones (order placed → shipped → delivered)
• One row per entity, updated as milestones occur
• Multiple date columns (order_date, ship_date, deliver_date)
• Useful for: pipeline monitoring, order fulfillment
15 ER modeling vs dimensional modeling? ER, dimensional • ER: entities and relationships, normalized, for OLTP
• Dimensional: facts and dimensions, denormalized, for OLAP
• ER: application-driven design
• Dimensional: query-driven design
16 Bridge tables? Bridge • Handle many-to-many between fact and dimension
• Example: one patient has many diagnoses, one diagnosis has many patients
• Bridge table sits between fact and dimension
• Contains weighting factor for proportional allocation
17 Role-playing dimensions? Role-playing • Same dimension table used multiple times with different meanings
• Example: date dimension as order_date, ship_date, delivery_date
• Implemented as views or aliases on same physical table
• Each role has its own foreign key in fact
18 Graph data modeling basics? Graph • Nodes (entities) + Edges (relationships) + Properties
• Best for: social networks, recommendation, fraud detection
• Tools: Neo4j, Neptune, JanusGraph
• Query language: Cypher (Neo4j), Gremlin (TinkerPop)
19 Document data modeling? Document • Schema-flexible, nested JSON/BSON documents
• Embed vs reference: embed for 1:few, reference for 1:many
• Denormalization is normal (optimize for read patterns)
• Tools: MongoDB, DynamoDB, Cosmos DB
20 How to model time-series data? Time-series • Partition by time (year/month/day) — most queries are time-ranged
• Wide vs narrow: wide (one row per entity per period) vs narrow (one row per measurement)
• Compression: columnar formats, delta encoding
• Tools: TimescaleDB, InfluxDB, Delta Lake

Part 21: dbt (Data Build Tool)¶

dbt Core Concepts¶

Concept Description
Model SQL SELECT statement that defines a transformation (saved as .sql file)
ref() Function to reference other models (builds DAG automatically)
source() Function to reference raw source tables (with freshness checks)
Materialization How model is persisted: table, view, incremental, ephemeral
Test Assertions about data: not_null, unique, accepted_values, relationships
Snapshot Captures SCD Type 2 changes over time
Macro Reusable SQL/Jinja template (like a function)
Package Reusable collection of models/macros (dbt-utils, dbt-expectations)

Materializations¶

Type How It Works Best For
view Creates SQL view (re-runs query each time) Light transformations, frequently changing logic
table Creates full table (drop and recreate) Final models, reports
incremental Appends/merges only new/changed rows Large fact tables, event data
ephemeral CTE injected into downstream models (no persistence) Reusable intermediate logic

dbt — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is dbt? dbt, transform • SQL-first transformation tool for analytics engineering
• T in ELT: transforms data already loaded in warehouse
• Version controlled, tested, documented SQL models
• Generates dependency DAG automatically from ref()
2 dbt Cloud vs dbt Core? Cloud, Core • Core: open-source CLI, free, self-managed
• Cloud: managed SaaS, IDE, scheduling, CI/CD, docs hosting
• Cloud adds: job orchestration, environment management, API
• Core for: teams with existing orchestration (Airflow)
3 How does incremental materialization work? Incremental • First run: full table build
• Subsequent runs: only process new/changed rows
• is_incremental() macro to add WHERE filter
• Strategy: append, merge, delete+insert
• unique_key for merge deduplication
4 dbt testing? Testing • Schema tests: not_null, unique, accepted_values, relationships
• Data tests: custom SQL returning failing rows
• dbt-expectations package: Great Expectations-style tests
• Test severity: error (fail build) vs warn (log only)
5 dbt snapshots for SCD? Snapshot, SCD • Captures Type 2 slowly changing dimensions
• Strategy: timestamp (updated_at) or check (compare columns)
• Adds: dbt_valid_from, dbt_valid_to, dbt_updated_at
• Runs as separate dbt snapshot command
6 Jinja in dbt? Jinja • Templating language embedded in SQL
• Variables: {{ var('my_var') }}
• Control flow: {% if %}, {% for %}
• Macros: reusable SQL templates
• Enables: dynamic SQL, DRY code, environment-specific logic
7 dbt packages? Packages • dbt-utils: generic tests, macros (surrogate_key, pivot)
• dbt-expectations: data quality tests
• codegen: auto-generate model YAML from sources
• Install via packages.yml and dbt deps
8 dbt sources and freshness? Sources, freshness • source() function references raw tables
• Define in YAML with database, schema, table
• Freshness: warn_after and error_after thresholds
• dbt source freshness command checks
9 dbt documentation and lineage? Docs, lineage • Auto-generated docs from YAML descriptions
• dbt docs generate + dbt docs serve
• DAG visualization shows model dependencies
• Column-level lineage with persist_docs config
10 dbt exposures? Exposures • Define downstream consumers (dashboards, ML models, apps)
• Documents: who uses this data and how
• Enables impact analysis when changing models
• Shows in dbt docs DAG alongside models
11 Medallion architecture in dbt? Medallion • Staging (stg_): 1:1 with source, rename, type cast
• Intermediate (int_): business logic, joins across sources
• Marts (mart_): final business-ready models grouped by domain
• Maps to Bronze/Silver/Gold in data lakehouse
12 How to handle large models in dbt? Large, performance • Use incremental materialization to avoid full rebuilds
• Cluster/partition target tables for query performance
• Split complex models into intermediate steps
• Use dbt-specific configurations (pre_hook, post_hook)
13 dbt CI/CD pipeline? CI/CD • PR: dbt build --select state:modified+ (only changed models)
• Slim CI: compare against production manifest
• GitHub Actions / GitLab CI / dbt Cloud CI
• Deploy to staging → production with environment configs
14 dbt vs Spark for transformations? dbt, Spark • dbt: SQL-first, warehouse-native, analytics engineering
• Spark: Python/Scala, handles unstructured data, ML
• dbt: simpler for SQL-heavy transforms, better testing
• Spark: streaming, complex ETL, non-SQL data
15 dbt seeds? Seeds • Load small CSV files directly into warehouse
• Good for: lookup tables, country codes, test fixtures
• Version controlled with project code
• Not for large datasets (use proper loading tools)

Part 22: Apache Iceberg & Hudi¶

Open Table Format Comparison¶

Feature Delta Lake Apache Iceberg Apache Hudi
Creator Databricks Netflix → Apache Uber → Apache
ACID Yes Yes Yes
Time Travel Yes (versioned) Yes (snapshot-based) Yes (timeline)
Schema Evolution Add/rename columns Full (add, rename, drop, reorder) Limited
Partition Evolution No (must rewrite) Yes (hidden partitioning) Limited
Engine Support Spark (best), Trino Spark, Trino, Flink, Presto (broad) Spark, Flink, Presto
Ecosystem Databricks-centric Engine-agnostic Uber/AWS-centric

Apache Iceberg & Hudi — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 What is Apache Iceberg? Iceberg • Open table format for large-scale analytics
• Created by Netflix, now Apache project
• Engine-agnostic: works with Spark, Trino, Flink, Presto
• Features: ACID, time travel, schema evolution, hidden partitioning
2 Iceberg architecture? Architecture • Metadata layer: metadata files → manifest lists → manifests → data files
• Manifest: tracks data files with column-level stats (min/max)
• Snapshot: atomic view of table at a point in time
• Catalog: tracks current metadata pointer
3 Hidden partitioning in Iceberg? Hidden, partition • Users don't need to know partition scheme in queries
• Partition transforms: year(), month(), day(), hour(), bucket(), truncate()
• Evolve partitions without rewriting data
• Eliminates wrong partition key mistakes in queries
4 Iceberg schema evolution? Schema, evolution • Add, drop, rename, reorder, widen columns without rewrite
• Uses unique column IDs (not names/positions)
• Safe: renaming column doesn't break existing data
• Strongest schema evolution of all open table formats
5 What is Apache Hudi? Hudi • Hadoop Upserts Deletes and Incrementals
• Created by Uber for incremental data processing
• Two table types: Copy-on-Write (COW) and Merge-on-Read (MOR)
• Strong CDC and incremental query support
6 Hudi COW vs MOR? COW, MOR • COW: rewrite entire file on update (fast reads, slow writes)
• MOR: write deltas to log files, merge on read (fast writes, slower reads)
• COW for: read-heavy, fewer updates
• MOR for: write-heavy, frequent upserts
7 Delta Lake vs Iceberg vs Hudi? Compare, formats • Delta: best in Databricks, strong community, simpler
• Iceberg: most engine-agnostic, best schema/partition evolution
• Hudi: best incremental processing, strong CDC
• Trend: convergence — all adding each other's features
8 When to choose Iceberg? Choose, Iceberg • Multi-engine environment (Spark + Trino + Flink)
• Need partition evolution without data rewrite
• Complex schema evolution requirements
• Want vendor-neutral open format
9 Iceberg time travel? Time travel • Each write creates new snapshot (atomic)
• Query historical snapshots: SELECT * FROM table VERSION AS OF <snapshot-id>
• Expire snapshots to manage storage
• Rollback to previous snapshot on errors
10 Compaction in Hudi? Compaction • MOR tables: merge log files into base columnar files
• Reduces read amplification over time
• Scheduled compaction (async or inline)
• Balance between write speed and read performance
11 Iceberg catalogs? Catalog • Hive Metastore, AWS Glue, Nessie, REST catalog
• Catalog tracks current metadata location
• Nessie: Git-like branching for table metadata
• REST catalog: vendor-neutral, growing standard
12 Data skipping in Iceberg? Data skipping • Column-level min/max stats in manifest files
• Skip data files that can't contain matching data
• Much faster than Hive partition pruning
• Bloom filters for high-cardinality columns
13 Iceberg merge-on-read? Merge on read • Delete files (positional or equality) mark rows as deleted
• Reads merge data files with delete files
• Avoids expensive full file rewrite on delete/update
• Compaction merges periodically for read performance
14 Hudi timeline and incremental queries? Timeline, incremental • Timeline: ordered log of all table operations
• Incremental queries: read only changes since last checkpoint
• Enables efficient CDC-style downstream processing
• Each commit has instant time for ordering
15 Migration to open table format? Migration • Delta: CONVERT TO DELTA from Parquet/Hive
• Iceberg: CALL catalog.migrate('table') from Hive
• In-place migration possible (metadata overlay on existing files)
• Gradual approach: dual-write during transition

Part 23: Snowflake¶

Snowflake Architecture¶

Layer Description
Cloud Services Authentication, metadata, query optimization, security
Compute (Virtual Warehouses) Independent clusters that execute queries (scale up/out)
Storage Centralized cloud storage (S3/ADLS/GCS), columnar micro-partitions

Key Concepts¶

Concept Description
Micro-partition 50-500MB compressed columnar files (automatically created)
Clustering key Defines sort order within micro-partitions for pruning
Time Travel Query data as of past time (up to 90 days on Enterprise)
Fail-safe 7-day recovery after Time Travel expires (Snowflake support only)
Zero-copy clone Instant clone of table/schema/database (no data duplication)
Snowpipe Continuous auto-ingestion from cloud storage
Data Sharing Share live data across accounts without copying
Snowpark DataFrame API for Python/Java/Scala in Snowflake

Snowflake — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Snowflake architecture? Architecture • Three-layer: Cloud Services + Compute + Storage
• Compute and storage scale independently
• Multi-cluster shared data: multiple warehouses access same data
• Runs natively on AWS, Azure, GCP
2 Virtual warehouses? Warehouse, compute • Independent compute clusters (XS to 6XL)
• Auto-suspend after idle timeout (saves cost)
• Auto-resume on query arrival
• Multi-cluster: auto-scale out for concurrency
3 Micro-partitions vs traditional partitions? Micro-partition • Automatic: no manual partitioning needed
• 50-500MB compressed columnar files
• Metadata tracks min/max values per column per micro-partition
• Enables automatic pruning without manual intervention
4 Clustering keys? Clustering • Define sort order for micro-partitions
• Improves pruning for common query filters
• Automatic re-clustering in background
• Cost trade-off: clustering credits vs query savings
5 Time Travel in Snowflake? Time Travel • Query past data: SELECT * FROM t AT(TIMESTAMP => '...')
• UNDROP table or schema
• Standard: 1 day; Enterprise: up to 90 days
• Storage cost for retained data versions
6 Zero-copy cloning? Clone • CREATE TABLE t_clone CLONE t
• Instant: metadata-only operation, no data copied
• Changes to clone don't affect original (copy-on-write)
• Use for: dev/test environments, safe experimentation
7 Snowpipe? Snowpipe, ingest • Continuous auto-ingestion from S3/ADLS/GCS
• Event-driven: triggered by cloud storage notifications
• Serverless: Snowflake manages compute
• Near real-time: seconds-level latency
8 Data Sharing in Snowflake? Sharing • Share live data without copying or ETL
• Provider creates share; consumer creates database from share
• Reader accounts for non-Snowflake consumers
• Snowflake Marketplace: discover and access third-party data
9 Snowflake vs Redshift? Snowflake, Redshift • Snowflake: true separation of compute/storage, auto-scaling
• Redshift: tightly coupled, manual scaling, cheaper for steady workloads
• Snowflake: easier to manage, higher cost per query
• Redshift Serverless: closing the gap
10 Snowpark? Snowpark • DataFrame API for Python, Java, Scala executed in Snowflake
• Push-down compute: code runs in Snowflake, not client
• UDFs and stored procedures in Python
• Enables ML/data engineering without moving data out
11 Streams and Tasks? Streams, Tasks • Streams: CDC on Snowflake tables (track inserts/updates/deletes)
• Tasks: scheduled SQL execution (cron-like)
• Together: incremental data pipelines within Snowflake
• Serverless tasks available
12 Snowflake cost optimization? Cost • Auto-suspend idle warehouses (set short timeout)
• Right-size warehouses for workload
• Use resource monitors for spend alerts/limits
• Clustering keys reduce scan, lowering credit usage
13 External tables in Snowflake? External • Query data in cloud storage without loading
• Supports: Parquet, ORC, JSON, CSV, Avro
• Slower than native tables (no micro-partition optimization)
• Use with materialized views for caching
14 Snowflake roles and access control? Roles, RBAC • Role-based access control (RBAC)
• Hierarchy: ACCOUNTADMIN → SYSADMIN → custom roles
• Column-level and row-level security
• Dynamic data masking for PII protection
15 Snowflake vs Databricks? Snowflake, Databricks • Snowflake: SQL-first, easier for analysts, strong data sharing
• Databricks: notebook-first, better for ML/data science, open formats
• Snowflake: closed format; Databricks: Delta Lake (open)
• Both converging: Snowpark vs SQL Analytics

Part 24: Data Quality & Observability¶

Data Quality Dimensions¶

Dimension Description Example Check
Completeness No missing values where expected NOT NULL checks, row count validation
Accuracy Values match reality Referential integrity, business rules
Consistency Same values across systems Cross-source reconciliation
Timeliness Data available when needed Freshness checks (max age)
Uniqueness No unwanted duplicates Primary key uniqueness
Validity Values within expected ranges Email format, age 0-150, date ranges

Data Quality & Observability Tools¶

Tool Type Key Feature
Great Expectations Open-source Expectations as code, data docs, checkpoints
Soda Core Open-source YAML-based checks, Soda Cloud for monitoring
dbt tests Built into dbt Schema tests + data tests integrated in transformation
Monte Carlo Commercial ML-based anomaly detection, automated monitoring
Elementary Open-source + dbt dbt-native observability, anomaly detection

Data Quality — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Data quality dimensions? Quality, dimensions • Completeness, accuracy, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, validity
• Each dimension needs specific checks and metrics
• Prioritize based on business impact
• Automate checks at each pipeline layer
2 What is Great Expectations? GE, expectations • Open-source data quality framework
• Define "expectations" (assertions about data) in Python
• Checkpoints: run expectations and generate data docs
• Integrates with Airflow, Spark, Pandas, SQL
3 Where to place quality checks in pipeline? Pipeline, checks • Source: validate incoming data before processing
• After each transformation layer (Bronze → Silver → Gold)
• Before serving: final validation before dashboard/ML
• Fail fast: block bad data early to prevent propagation
4 Data observability vs data quality? Observability • Quality: active checks (are expectations met?)
• Observability: passive monitoring (detect anomalies automatically)
• Observability pillars: freshness, volume, schema, distribution, lineage
• Both needed: quality prevents, observability detects
5 Data contracts? Contracts • Agreement between producer and consumer on data shape
• Defines: schema, SLAs (freshness, completeness), ownership
• Enforce via: schema registry, CI/CD validation, runtime checks
• Breaking changes require contract negotiation
6 Schema validation strategies? Schema, validation • Schema registry (Confluent): enforce at publish time
• Delta Lake: schema enforcement rejects incompatible writes
• Schema evolution: mergeSchema for backward-compatible changes
• Validate in CI/CD: compare schemas before deploy
7 Row count reconciliation? Reconciliation • Compare source row count vs target after each pipeline run
• Track row counts at each layer (Bronze/Silver/Gold)
• Alert on unexpected drops (>5% decrease) or spikes
• Essential for: migrations, new pipeline validation
8 How to handle data quality failures? Failure, handling • Quarantine: route bad data to dead-letter table for investigation
• Circuit breaker: stop pipeline if error rate exceeds threshold
• Alert: notify data team via Slack/PagerDuty
• Retry with backoff for transient failures
9 Data freshness monitoring? Freshness • Track: when was table last updated?
• Alert if: table not refreshed within SLA window
• Tools: dbt source freshness, Monte Carlo, Elementary
• Metadata table: log pipeline completion timestamps
10 Data lineage for quality? Lineage, quality • End-to-end tracking: source → transformations → target
• Impact analysis: which dashboards affected by upstream issue?
• Root cause: trace quality failure back to source
• Tools: OpenLineage, DataHub, Purview, Unity Catalog

Part 25: Data Engineering Terminologies¶

DE Terminologies — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 ETL vs ELT? ETL, ELT • ETL: Extract→Transform→Load (transform before loading)
• ELT: Extract→Load→Transform (transform in warehouse)
• ELT dominant in cloud (cheap compute in warehouse)
• ETL for: data quality before loading
2 Batch vs stream processing? Batch, stream • Batch: process bounded datasets on schedule (hourly/daily)
• Stream: process unbounded data in real-time
• Batch: simpler, higher latency; Stream: complex, low latency
• Micro-batch: middle ground (Spark Streaming)
3 Schema-on-read vs schema-on-write? Schema, read, write • Schema-on-write: enforce schema at write time (RDBMS, Delta)
• Schema-on-read: infer schema at read time (raw data lakes)
• Schema-on-write: better data quality, faster queries
• Schema-on-read: flexible ingestion
4 Data lineage — what and why? Lineage • Track data from source through transformations to target
• Answers: where data came from, how it was transformed
• Required for: compliance (GDPR), debugging, impact analysis
• Tools: Purview, DataHub, Unity Catalog, OpenLineage
5 Medallion architecture (Bronze/Silver/Gold)? Medallion • Bronze: raw, as-is data (append-only)
• Silver: cleaned, validated, deduplicated (analytics-ready)
• Gold: aggregated, business-specific KPIs (BI/ML-ready)
• Progressive quality improvement
6 Data mesh vs data fabric? Mesh, fabric • Data Mesh: organizational — domain teams own data products
• Data Fabric: technical — AI-driven data integration layer
• Mesh: people-centric, decentralized
• Fabric: technology-centric, automated
7 Docker in data engineering? Docker • Package pipeline code + dependencies in containers
• Reproducible environments across dev/staging/prod
• Docker Compose: multi-service orchestration (Airflow + Postgres + Redis)
• Enables: local development matching production
8 CI/CD for data pipelines? CI/CD • CI: lint, test, validate on every code push
• CD: auto-deploy to staging → production
• Test: DAG parsing, schema validation, data quality
• Tools: GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, Jenkins
9 CDC (Change Data Capture) tools? CDC, tools • Debezium: open-source, Kafka-based CDC (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB)
• AWS DMS: managed CDC service
• Oracle GoldenGate: enterprise CDC
• Fivetran: managed ELT with CDC support
10 SCD (Slowly Changing Dimensions)? SCD, types • Type 1: overwrite (no history)
• Type 2: add row with version dates (full history)
• Type 3: add old/new column (limited history)
• Type 2 implemented with Delta MERGE
11 ACID properties? ACID • Atomicity: all-or-nothing transactions
• Consistency: data always valid after transaction
• Isolation: concurrent transactions don't interfere
• Durability: committed data survives crashes
12 CAP theorem? CAP • Consistency: all nodes see same data
• Availability: every request gets response
• Partition tolerance: system works despite network splits
• Can only guarantee 2 of 3: CP (HBase) or AP (Cassandra)
13 Idempotency in pipelines? Idempotent • Re-running pipeline produces same result (no duplicates)
• Use MERGE/upsert, not INSERT
• Use execution_date, not current timestamp
• Essential for: retries, backfills, fault recovery
14 Backpressure in streaming? Backpressure • Consumer can't keep up with producer's rate
• Symptoms: growing lag, increasing memory, OOM
• Solutions: scale consumers, rate-limit producers, buffer in Kafka
• Spark: auto-backpressure via rate source config
15 Data quality dimensions? Quality • Completeness: no missing values
• Accuracy: values match reality
• Consistency: same values across systems
• Timeliness: data available when needed
• Uniqueness: no duplicates
16 Data catalog vs data dictionary? Catalog, dictionary • Catalog: searchable inventory of all data assets (tables, files, APIs)
• Dictionary: detailed description of specific dataset's columns/types
• Catalog: org-wide discovery; Dictionary: dataset-level documentation
• Tools: DataHub, Amundsen, Alation
17 Data lakehouse — how does it unify? Lakehouse, unified • Single platform for: raw storage + ACID + SQL + ML
• Open formats (Delta/Iceberg) with warehouse features
• Replace: separate data lake + data warehouse
• Benefits: no data copying, unified governance
18 Serialization formats — Avro vs Parquet vs ORC? Serialization • Avro: row-based, great schema evolution, streaming (Kafka)
• Parquet: columnar, great for analytics (Spark ecosystem default)
• ORC: columnar, optimized for Hive (ACID support)
• Use Parquet/ORC for analytics; Avro for streaming
19 Data encryption — at rest vs in transit? Encryption • At rest: data stored encrypted on disk (AES-256, KMS keys)
• In transit: data encrypted over network (TLS/SSL)
• Both required for compliance (GDPR, HIPAA, SOX)
• Cloud services: usually default or one-click enable
20 Data partitioning strategies? Partition, strategy • Time-based: year/month/day (most common for event data)
• Hash-based: distribute evenly across buckets
• Range-based: ordered ranges (IDs, dates)
• Choose based on query patterns and cardinality
21 dbt (Data Build Tool) — why popular? dbt, transform • SQL-first transformation on top of warehouses
• Version controlled, tested, documented models
• Lineage DAG shows data dependencies
• Analytics engineering standard tool
22 Orchestration tools comparison? Orchestration • Airflow: mature, Python DAGs, large ecosystem
• Prefect: modern, dynamic, better error handling
• Dagster: asset-aware, type-safe, software engineering focus
• Databricks Workflows: native for Databricks
23 Data contracts — how to enforce? Contract, enforce • Schema registry: validate before publish
• CI/CD: check contract compliance in pipeline
• Tools: schemathesis, protobuf, json-schema
• SLAs: freshness, completeness, latency guarantees
24 Feature engineering vs feature store? Feature, engineering • Feature engineering: create ML input features from raw data
• Feature store: centralized repo for serving features
• Ensures train/serve consistency
• Tools: Feast, Databricks Feature Store, Tecton
25 Observability vs monitoring? Observability • Monitoring: predefined metrics and alerts
• Observability: ability to understand system state from outputs
• Observability pillars: metrics, logs, traces
• Data observability: freshness, volume, schema, distribution
26 Data governance — key components? Governance • Access control: who can access what data
• Data quality: rules and validation
• Compliance: GDPR, HIPAA, SOX adherence
• Cataloging: discover and document all data assets
27 Terraform for data infrastructure? Terraform, IaC • Define cloud resources in HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language)
• Multi-cloud support: AWS, Azure, GCP
• Plan→Apply workflow (preview changes before deploying)
• State file tracks current infrastructure
28 Data retention policies? Retention, policy • How long to keep data before archiving/deleting
• Compliance: GDPR requires deletion, SOX requires 7-year retention
• Implement: VACUUM (Delta), S3 lifecycle, TTL (HBase/Cassandra)
• Balance: compliance + cost + analytics needs
29 Reverse ETL — what is it? Reverse ETL • Push transformed data FROM warehouse TO operational tools
• Warehouse → CRM, marketing, customer support, product
• Tools: Census, Hightouch, Rudderstack
• Closes the loop: analytics insights → operational action
30 Data product — what defines one? Data product • Owned by a domain team (data mesh principle)
• Discoverable, addressable, trustworthy, self-describing
• Has SLAs, documentation, quality guarantees
• Consumed by other teams via well-defined interfaces

Part 26: System Design for Data Engineers¶

System Design — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Design a real-time analytics dashboard system. Real-time, dashboard • Ingest: Kafka for event ingestion from web/mobile apps
• Process: Spark Structured Streaming for aggregation
• Store: Delta Lake (raw) + Druid/ClickHouse (serving layer)
• Serve: WebSocket/API → dashboard frontend
2 Design an ETL pipeline for e-commerce. ETL, e-commerce • Source: PostgreSQL (orders), S3 (clickstream CSV), API (inventory)
• Ingest: Debezium CDC → Kafka → S3 Bronze
• Transform: Spark/dbt → S3 Silver (join orders+inventory+clicks)
• Serve: S3 Gold → Redshift → Power BI dashboards
3 Design a log processing pipeline. Log, pipeline • Collect: Fluentd/Filebeat → Kafka topics
• Process: Spark Streaming for parsing, enrichment
• Store: ElasticSearch (search) + S3 (archive)
• Visualize: Kibana dashboards + alerts
4 Design a recommendation system data pipeline. Recommendation • Collect: user events (views, clicks, purchases) → Kafka
• Feature engineering: Spark → user profiles, item features
• Training: MLflow + Spark MLlib, store models in Feature Store
• Serving: real-time scoring via API, batch refresh daily
5 Design a data lake architecture. Data lake, design • Storage: ADLS Gen2 or S3 with medallion layers (B/S/G)
• Format: Delta Lake for ACID, versioning, data skipping
• Governance: Unity Catalog or Lake Formation for access control
• Orchestration: Airflow/ADF for scheduling
6 Design a CDC pipeline for microservices. CDC, microservices • Capture: Debezium connectors per microservice database
• Transport: Kafka topics per source table
• Consume: Spark/Flink reads from Kafka → Delta Lake
• Challenges: schema evolution, ordering, exactly-once
7 Design a data pipeline for ML feature store. Feature store • Raw data: event streams + batch sources → data lake
• Feature engineering: Spark SQL transforms
• Feature store: online (Redis/DynamoDB) + offline (Delta Lake)
• Serving: point-in-time lookups for training/prediction
8 Design a cost-effective data warehouse. Cost, warehouse • Use S3/ADLS for cold storage (cheapest)
• Athena/serverless SQL for ad-hoc queries (pay-per-query)
• Redshift/Synapse reserved for high-concurrency BI
• Lifecycle: archive old data to Glacier/cool tier
9 How to handle a 10x data volume increase? Scale, volume • Horizontal scaling: add more partitions/executors
• Optimize: partition pruning, broadcast joins, AQE
• Compress: switch to Parquet/ORC if using CSV
• Denormalize: avoid expensive joins
10 Design a streaming fraud detection system. Fraud, streaming • Ingest: transaction events → Kafka (sub-second)
• Process: Spark Streaming + ML model scoring
• Rules: geo-anomaly, velocity checks, amount thresholds
• Output: flagged transactions → alert system + Delta audit log
11 Design a multi-tenant data platform. Multi-tenant • Isolation: separate schemas/catalogs per tenant
• Access: RBAC via Unity Catalog/Lake Formation
• Compute: resource pools per tenant to prevent noisy neighbors
• Billing: track compute/storage per tenant
12 Design a data quality monitoring system. Quality, monitor • Validate at each layer: nulls, ranges, uniqueness, freshness
• Tools: Great Expectations embedded in pipeline
• Alerting: Slack/email when quality checks fail
• Dashboard: track quality metrics over time
13 Design a real-time IoT data pipeline. IoT, real-time • Ingest: IoT Hub/Event Hubs (millions of events/sec)
• Process: Spark Streaming / Azure Stream Analytics
• Store: Delta Lake (time-series), InfluxDB (metrics)
• Alert: threshold-based anomaly detection → notification
14 Design a data migration strategy (on-prem to cloud). Migration, cloud • Assess: inventory data, dependencies, SLAs
• Strategy: parallel run (both systems) during migration
• Tools: DMS/ADF for data, Terraform for infra
• Validate: data reconciliation between on-prem and cloud
15 Design a slowly changing dimension pipeline. SCD, pipeline • Source CDC: Debezium captures row changes
• Delta MERGE: match on business key, update/insert
• SCD Type 2: add start_date, end_date, is_current columns
• Schedule: Airflow daily or event-driven
16 Design a data governance framework. Governance, design • Catalog: auto-scan all sources → DataHub/Purview
• Classification: auto-tag PII columns
• Access: RBAC with column-level security
• Lineage: end-to-end tracking from source to dashboard
17 Design notification/alerting for pipeline failures. Alert, notification • Detect: Airflow callbacks, CloudWatch alarms, Spark listeners
• Route: SNS → Slack channel + PagerDuty for critical
• Context: include job name, error message, stack trace
• Runbook: link to troubleshooting documentation
18 Design a data pipeline for GDPR compliance. GDPR, compliance • Data catalog: identify all PII fields across systems
• Right to erasure: Delta DELETE + VACUUM for cleanup
• Consent management: track user consent per processing purpose
• Audit log: immutable record of all data access
19 Design a pipeline for A/B testing analytics. A/B test • Events: user assignments + actions → Kafka → Delta Lake
• Analysis: Spark SQL for experiment metrics (conversion, revenue)
• Statistics: chi-square, t-tests, confidence intervals
• Dashboard: experiment results with significance indicators
20 How would you rebuild a failed data pipeline? Rebuild, recovery • Identify: root cause from logs and monitoring
• Fix: address the code/data/infra issue
• Replay: backfill affected date range (idempotent design)
• Validate: data reconciliation + quality checks
• Prevent: add monitoring/tests for the failure mode

Part 27: Scenario-Based Interview Questions¶

Scenario-Based — Interview Questions¶

# Question Keywords Answer
1 Your Spark job OOMs. How do you debug? OOM, debug • Check Spark UI for skewed partitions or large shuffle
• Increase executor memory or repartition data
• Avoid collect() on large DataFrames
• Use broadcast join for small table joins
2 Data appears duplicated in output. Root cause? Duplicate, debug • Check: was pipeline re-run without idempotent writes?
• Check: Kafka at-least-once without dedup downstream?
• Fix: MERGE/upsert, dropDuplicates with window function
• Prevention: idempotent design + dedup at Silver layer
3 Pipeline takes 4 hours but needs to run in 1 hour. Slow, optimize • Profile: Spark UI → identify slowest stages
• Optimize: broadcast joins, reduce shuffles, partition pruning
• Scale: more executors, enable AQE, tune parallelism
• Architecture: can parts run in parallel instead of sequential?
4 Source schema changed unexpectedly. What happens? Schema, change • Schema enforcement (Delta) rejects incompatible writes
• Without enforcement: silent data corruption or nulls
• Fix: schema evolution with mergeSchema for additions
• Prevention: data contracts, schema registry validation
5 Customer asks to delete their data (GDPR). How? GDPR, delete • Locate all PII across Delta tables (data catalog)
• Delta DELETE WHERE customer_id = x
• VACUUM to physically remove old files
• Verify deletion + audit log documentation
6 Your Kafka consumer lags 2 hours behind. What to do? Kafka, lag • Check consumer processing speed (is it bottleneck?)
• Scale: add more consumers to the consumer group
• Increase partitions (if consumer count > partitions, no effect)
• Optimize consumer: batch processing, skip deserialization of unused fields
7 Airflow DAG hasn't triggered for 3 days. Why? Airflow, not running • Check scheduler is running: airflow jobs check
• Check DAG is unpaused in UI
• Check start_date is in the past + schedule_interval set
• Check task dependencies — upstream sensor might be timing out
8 Data lake costs are growing 30% monthly. How to control? Cost, growing • Lifecycle policies: archive old data to cold storage
• VACUUM Delta tables to remove old versions
• Compact small files (OPTIMIZE) to reduce metadata overhead
• Review: are unused tables/pipelines still writing data?
9 Two teams need same data but different schemas. Solution? Schema, teams • Medallion: shared Silver layer + team-specific Gold views
• Materialized views per team's requirements
• Data products: one source, different interfaces
• Avoid duplicating ETL — transform at serving layer
10 Spark join produces 10x expected output rows. Why? Join, explosion • Many-to-many join: both sides have duplicate keys
• Check: are join keys truly unique on at least one side?
• Fix: deduplicate before join, or use semi join
• Verify: df.groupBy('key').count().filter('count > 1')
11 How to handle 500GB daily file landing in S3? Large file, ingest • Split ingestion: Autoloader or Glue with bookmarks
• Process in parallel: Spark with multiple partitions
• Incremental: process only new files since last run
• Format: convert CSV → Parquet at Bronze layer immediately
12 Dashboard shows stale data (12h old). How to reduce? Stale, freshness • Identify bottleneck: ingestion, processing, or serving?
• Move from batch (daily) to micro-batch (hourly/15-min)
• Streaming: Structured Streaming + Delta for near real-time
• Caching: refresh materialized views more frequently
13 Your Delta table has 100K small files. How to fix? Small files, Delta • Run OPTIMIZE to compact into larger files (target ~256MB)
• Enable auto-compaction in Databricks
• Review upstream: coalesce before write, reduce partitions
• For streaming: increase trigger interval, batch writes
14 Spark job runs fine with 1GB but fails with 100GB. How to fix? Scale, failure • Increase spark.sql.shuffle.partitions (default 200 too few)
• Use broadcast join for small lookup tables
• Enable AQE for dynamic optimization
• Check for data skew — salt the skewed keys
15 You need to migrate from Hive to Spark SQL. Strategy? Migrate, Hive • Phase 1: point Spark to Hive Metastore (read Hive tables)
• Phase 2: rewrite HiveQL as SparkSQL (mostly compatible)
• Phase 3: convert data to Delta Lake format (CONVERT TO DELTA)
• Phase 4: move from MapReduce execution to Spark
16 Pipeline works in dev but fails in prod. Why? Dev, prod • Data volume: prod has 100x more data (OOM, shuffles)
• Schema: prod has edge cases not in dev sample
• Permissions: prod has stricter IAM/ACLs
• Fix: test with prod-like data volumes in staging
17 How to handle timezone differences in global data? Timezone • Store all timestamps in UTC
• Convert to local timezone only at presentation layer
• Partition by UTC date to avoid confusion
• Document timezone conventions in data dictionary
18 Your pipeline processes 100M rows. How to ensure quality? Quality, large • Automated checks: Great Expectations / dbt tests at each layer
• Row counts: compare source vs target (no data loss)
• Sample validation: spot-check random samples manually
• Null ratios, unique counts, value distributions
19 Need to join a 1TB table with a 10MB table. Best approach? Join, optimization • Broadcast join: send 10MB table to all executors
• hint: df_large.join(F.broadcast(df_small), 'key')
• Avoid sort-merge join (shuffles 1TB!)
• Verify with explain() that BroadcastHashJoin is used
20 How to implement incremental data loading? Incremental, load • Timestamp-based: load rows WHERE updated_at > last_run
• CDC-based: Debezium captures only changes
• Glue bookmarks: auto-track last processed position
• Delta CDF: track row-level changes between versions
21 You discover PII in an unencrypted table. Next steps? PII, security • Immediate: restrict access to the table
• Mask/tokenize PII columns or move to encrypted storage
• Report: inform data governance/security team
• Prevent: add PII scanning to catalog, set up alerts
22 A downstream report shows wrong totals. How to debug? Debug, wrong • Trace lineage: identify all transformations from source to report
• Compare at each layer: Bronze→Silver→Gold→Report
• Check: join fanout, null handling in aggregations, filter conditions
• Fix: add data quality checks at each layer boundary
23 Need to process 5 years of historical data. Approach? Backfill, historical • Partition by date: process one month at a time (avoid OOM)
• Parallel backfill: submit parallel jobs per date range
• Idempotent writes: safe to re-run failed date ranges
• Monitor: track completion per partition
24 Your streaming pipeline has increasing latency. Why? Latency, streaming • Check: is input rate exceeding processing capacity?
• Check: state store growing (missing watermarks?)
• Scale: increase Spark executors or Kafka consumers
• Optimize: reduce stateful operations, add watermarks
25 How to implement row-level security in data lake? Row-level, security • Delta Lake + Unity Catalog: row filters per group
• Views with WHERE clause filtering by user context
• Apache Ranger policies on Hive/Spark tables
• Lake Formation: cell-level security on AWS
26 Your team debates Airflow vs Databricks Workflows. Advice? Airflow, Databricks • Airflow: multi-platform, open-source, large ecosystem
• Workflows: native Databricks integration, simpler for DB-only
• Airflow if: orchestrating non-Databricks services
• Workflows if: everything runs in Databricks
27 How to handle a corrupt Parquet file in production? Corrupt, Parquet • Identify: which partition/file using Spark error logs
• Remove: delete corrupt file from storage
• Repair: Delta: recreate from transaction log; Parquet: reprocess from source
• Prevent: enable checksums, validate writes
28 Manager wants real-time analytics but budget is limited. Budget, real-time • Near-real-time with micro-batch (5-15 min delay, much cheaper)
• Use serverless: Kinesis Firehose→Athena, Event Hubs→Synapse Serverless
• Avoid always-on streaming clusters
• Trigger(availableNow): batch-like streaming for cost control
29 How to validate a data migration? Validate, migration • Row count comparison: source vs target per table
• Checksum: hash aggregate values for data integrity
• Sample spot checks: compare random rows column-by-column
• Regression: run existing reports/queries on both systems
30 Your Delta table time travel shows unexpected changes. How to investigate? Time travel, investigate • DESCRIBE HISTORY table: see all operations + users + timestamps
• Compare versions: read two versions, find diff
• Check transaction log: _delta_log JSON files for add/remove actions
• Audit: identify who/what made the problematic change
31 Your Spark checkpoint gets corrupted. Recovery? Checkpoint, corrupt • Delete corrupt checkpoint directory
• Restart from last known good offset (Kafka) or file position
• If using Delta: recover from transaction log
• Prevention: checkpoint to durable storage (S3/ADLS), not local disk
32 Source system sends duplicate primary keys. How to handle? Duplicate, keys • Dedup at ingestion: window function ROW_NUMBER + ORDER BY timestamp
• Pick latest record per key using QUALIFY or subquery
• Implement at Silver layer (Bronze keeps everything)
• Alert if dup rate exceeds threshold
33 Need to deprecate a widely-used table. Strategy? Deprecate, migration • Announce timeline: deprecation notice with deadline
• Create new table alongside old; dual-write during transition
• Track consumers: who queries the old table?
• Soft-deprecate (views/aliases) before hard removal
34 Your data lake is a data swamp. How to clean up? Swamp, governance • Audit: inventory all tables, identify owners, track usage
• Implement medallion architecture (organize raw/curated/consumed)
• Governance: catalog all assets, enforce naming conventions
• Lifecycle: auto-archive unused data, delete stale tables
35 Two pipelines write to same table concurrently. Conflicts? Concurrent, conflict • Delta Lake: optimistic concurrency with transaction log
• Conflict resolution: retry with latest version
• Partition by non-overlapping keys (each pipeline owns partitions)
• Alternative: merge into single pipeline with event-driven trigger
36 Client wants exactly-once delivery across pipeline. How? Exactly-once • End-to-end exactly-once is hard; aim for effectively-once
• Kafka: idempotent producer + transactional consumer
• Spark: checkpoint + idempotent sink (Delta MERGE)
• Use deduplication at destination as safety net
37 Data arrives in 500 different CSV schemas. Handling? Schema, variety • Schema inference with spark.read.option('inferSchema', true)
• Schema registry: catalog known schemas, flag new ones
• Auto-mapping: canonical model with ETL per source type
• Reject and quarantine files with unknown schemas
38 Compliance requires 7-year data retention but fast queries. Retention, archive • Hot-warm-cold architecture: recent in fast storage, old in archive
• S3 lifecycle: move to Glacier after X months
• Partition by date for easy lifecycle management
• Aggregate old data (daily → monthly summary) for query performance
39 Your Airflow DAG has 200 tasks and is slow. Optimization? DAG, optimization • Reduce tasks: combine small tasks into larger ones
• Use pools to limit concurrent database connections
• Sensor mode='reschedule' instead of 'poke' (frees worker)
• Sub-DAGs or TaskGroups for logical organization
40 Team argues about Spark vs Flink for new streaming pipeline. Decision, streaming • Ask: what's the latency requirement? (sub-second → Flink; seconds → Spark)
• Team expertise: existing Spark skills favor Spark Streaming
• Ecosystem: ML integration → Spark; complex CEP → Flink
• Hybrid: Flink for streaming, Spark for batch
41 Need to load 10TB of Parquet into Snowflake. Strategy? Load, Snowflake • Stage files in S3/ADLS cloud storage
• COPY INTO with multiple warehouses for parallel load
• Pre-sort data to match clustering keys
• Use XL warehouse for load, then resize for queries
42 Data shows sales spiked 10x on a random Tuesday. Debug? Anomaly, debug • Check source: did upstream system have a bug/duplicate push?
• Compare row counts source vs target at each layer
• Check join logic: fanout from many-to-many?
• Verify date/timezone handling: wrong day? UTC vs local?
43 Need CDC from a legacy database without log access. CDC, legacy • Timestamp-based CDC: WHERE updated_at > last_run_time
• Full-snapshot comparison: hash current vs previous load
• Trigger-based: add DB triggers to log changes (invasive)
• Application-level: event sourcing from application logs
44 Spark job works on Databricks but fails on EMR. Why? Cross-platform • Check: Spark version mismatch (different distro versions)
• Dependencies: different library versions (Hadoop, Hive)
• Configs: Databricks has custom defaults (AQE settings, memory)
• Delta Lake: native on Databricks, needs manual setup on EMR
45 Manager wants a "real-time dashboard." What to clarify? Requirements • Define "real-time": sub-second? minutes? hourly?
• Cost vs latency trade-off discussion
• Data freshness SLA: 1-minute delay often sufficient
• Suggest: near-real-time micro-batch (cheaper, simpler)
46 How to unit test a Spark transformation? Testing, Spark • Use PySpark with local mode in pytest
• Create small test DataFrames with known input/output
• Test transformation function, assert result matches expected
• Libraries: chispa (DataFrame comparison), great_expectations
47 Need to join 3 billion-row tables without shuffling. Join, no shuffle • Bucket join: both tables bucketed on join key, same # buckets
• Pre-partition: both tables partitioned on join key
• Broadcast one if small enough after filtering
• Sort-merge join with AQE for dynamic optimization
48 Data team of 3 manages 200 pipelines. Scaling advice? Scale, team • Standardize: templates for common pipeline patterns
• Self-service: parameterized pipelines, data contracts
• dbt for SQL transforms (analysts can self-serve)
• Invest in monitoring/alerting to reduce firefighting
49 How to handle a pipeline that runs for 12 hours? Long-running • Break into smaller incremental jobs (hourly batches)
• Profile: identify bottleneck stages (Spark UI)
• Checkpoint intermediate results for restart capability
• Consider streaming for continuous processing vs big batch
50 Production table schema change needed. Deployment strategy? Schema change • Backward-compatible first: add new columns, keep old ones
• Migration plan: update writers → backfill → update readers → drop old columns
• Use schema evolution (mergeSchema in Delta/Iceberg)
• Feature flags: toggle between old/new schema
51 How to handle nested JSON in a data pipeline? JSON, nested • Spark: explode() for arrays, struct.field_name for nested objects
• Flatten to tabular at Silver layer
• Schema inference: spark.read.json with multiLine=true
• Handle schema evolution: permissive mode + column merging
52 Data from API has rate limits. How to ingest efficiently? API, rate limit • Respect rate limits: exponential backoff with jitter
• Batch requests: use bulk API endpoints if available
• Cache: store results, avoid redundant calls
• Async ingestion: queue requests, process within limits
53 How to build a cost-effective data platform from scratch? Green field, cost • Start simple: cloud storage + serverless SQL (Athena/Synapse Serverless)
• Add orchestration when >5 pipelines (Airflow/dbt Cloud)
• Invest in governance early (catalog, naming conventions)
• Scale compute on-demand; avoid always-on clusters
54 Your dbt model takes 3 hours to build. Fix? dbt, slow • Change materialization: incremental instead of table
• Profile: check if underlying warehouse query is slow
• Break into smaller models with intermediate materializations
• Warehouse optimization: clustering keys, larger warehouse size
55 How to handle data from 50 different source systems? Multi-source • Standardize: common ingestion pattern per source type
• Canonical data model: map each source to common schema
• Metadata-driven: config tables define source → target mapping
• Quality: source-specific validation rules
56 Need to implement data lineage across your platform. Approach? Lineage, platform • Tools: OpenLineage (open standard), DataHub, Purview
• Integrate with: Spark (OpenLineage agent), Airflow, dbt
• Capture: column-level lineage, transformation logic
• Visualize: end-to-end from source to dashboard
57 Streaming pipeline has late data arriving hours later. Handling? Late data, stream • Watermarks: define how late data can be (e.g., 2 hours)
• Side outputs: route very late data for reprocessing
• Delta Lake: upsert late records into existing partitions
• Batch correction job: reconcile next day
58 How to implement data masking for PII? Masking, PII • Dynamic masking: Snowflake masking policies, Databricks column masks
• Static masking: SHA-256 hash PII at Bronze → Silver boundary
• Role-based: raw PII for compliance team, masked for analysts
• Detect PII: automated scanning (Purview, Macie)
59 Your Delta table has 5 million small files. Recovery? Small files, Delta • OPTIMIZE with ZORDER for both compaction and co-location
• Enable auto-compaction: autoCompact + optimizedWrite
• Root cause: reduce upstream micro-batching frequency
• Schedule VACUUM to remove old files after retention
60 Need to migrate from Hive Metastore to Unity Catalog. Migration, Unity • Phase 1: inventory all databases, tables, permissions in Hive
• Phase 2: create corresponding catalogs/schemas in Unity
• Phase 3: SYNC commands or manual table migration
• Phase 4: update all queries/pipelines to new three-level namespace
